L14 lists this row as its stance capability, so the generated SKILL.md would instruct the legacy pattern.

verdict.reason: RND.ARCH.scene-sync text says per-frame mirrored copy of every scene object, O(scene objects), directly contradicting C-RSCENE and L14 (which lists it as stance capability); the proposed reword is sound.

findings.proposed_change: Set RND.GI.restir to M with aaa tag; make RND.GI.hybrid the std3d default; merge/rename the duplicate radar entries.

findings.finding: Cluster assemblies and virtualized foliage are E while sibling deforming LOD and displacement (same source, earlier) are M; they are experimental/beta in the reference engine and enter std3d by default without radar coverage.

findings.proposed_change: Split path-tracing targets (reference -> tools/test only), tag RND.PT.reference 'tools' and RT provider rows std3d/rt; add check that dev-only capabilities never resolve into client targets.

verdict.reason: Model confirms lite-3d-mobile-client and lite-3d-web-client include path-tracing and ray-tracing-infrastructure and RND.PT.reference (dev-only) resolves there, a genuine scale-down over-inclusion, but the 'breaches L52' framing (console/ports/live coding) is overstated so major is inflated.

verdict.reason: No capability covers cell-streamed baked lighting/probe volumes/scenario blending (RND.TOOL.lighting authors scenarios only) and the RES.MGMT.arbitration pool list omits lighting data, a real omission for lite3d/open-world baked GI.

findings.finding: CORE.JOBS.degenerate allows blocking waits on the host thread for IO completion. RES.MGMT.no-stall forbids blocking on host/OS-bound threads and CORE.FRAME.host-loop requires a non-blocking cooperative frame step. On the browser main thread Atomics.wait is disallowed and a sync wait starves the event loop that delivers the completion.
findings.evidence: HTML/WASM threading rules: the main thread cannot block, and fetch/OPFS completions arrive on the event loop. Mobile watchdogs also kill a blocked main thread.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite CORE.JOBS.degenerate: in host-driven mode IO and GPU completions arrive only as event-loop callbacks converted to C-TASK tokens, and no wait primitive is legal on the host thread. Permit blocking waits only in non-host-driven cooperative targets. Add a C-TASK conformance case: a 0-worker host-driven graph completes a load with no blocking wait.

verdict.reason: CORE.JOBS.degenerate literally allows blocking waits on the host thread while RES.MGMT.no-stall and CORE.FRAME.host-loop forbid them, and on the web main thread a blocking wait cannot succeed; the rewrite is sound.

findings.finding: There is no storage-class dimension. Tiers, IO scheduling and IO-bandwidth arbitration assume NVMe-like random access. Rotational disks, SD cards, eMMC/UFS, cartridges and network volumes need seek-aware ordering, low queue depth, duplication or clustering policy and different streaming budgets. C-BUDGET has no sustained-read or IOPS line per storage class.
findings.evidence: Cyberpunk 2077 and Spider-Man PC HDD hitching. Helldivers 2 dropping HDD asset duplication. Steam Deck SD-card load variance. DirectStorage and GPU decompression are NVMe-gated.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.PAL.storage-class (rotational/SATA-SSD/NVMe/removable/network, with a throughput and latency probe). Add RES.IO.media-policy owned by async-io-storage, with package-formats-vfs contributing to layout. Add a storage-class axis to tier records and sustained-read and IOPS lines to C-BUDGET. Feed the probe into RES.MGMT.arbitration.

verdict.reason: No storage-class, HDD, SD or seek-aware capability exists anywhere (only a bare 'storage' word in PAL.system-events), and C-BUDGET has no sustained-read or IOPS line; the addition is sound and not excluded by any recorded scope decision.

findings.finding: Two owners define event delivery ordering: entity-object-model (CORE.OBJ.events, deferred batched delivery at consumption points) and frame-orchestration (CORE.FRAME.channels, gameplay event dispatch, subscriptions and delivery ordering). Neither row lists the other. Ordering across the two mechanisms is unowned, which undermines replay and rollback determinism.
findings.evidence: Replay determinism (C-DET) needs a single ordering authority. Bevy and Unity DOTS route events through one mechanism scheduled by the same access graph.
findings.proposed_change: Make CORE.FRAME.channels the sole mechanism and ordering authority. Redefine CORE.OBJ.events as event type/ID/payload schema only and add frame-orchestration as contributor. State in C-FLOW that GAM.SYS.messages and PHY.ARCH.events are channel producers.

verdict.reason: CORE.OBJ.events (entity-object-model) and CORE.FRAME.channels (frame-orchestration) both define event delivery with no cross-listing and no single ordering authority, which matters for C-DET replay.

findings.finding: Ownership policy is split across three owners. C-LIFETIME (concurrency-primitives) claims the engine-wide ownership and cross-thread reference rules, while the same-worded row CORE.LIFE.ownership-model belongs to core-runtime-architect. CORE.OBJ.references and C-ID also own reference kinds and lifetime rules. An agent changing a rule cannot tell which contract change request to file, and the mechanism implementer authors the policy it consumes.
findings.evidence: A single policy owner is standard practice, as in Rust ownership rules and Unreal's split between UObject and raw pointer ownership. Retirement mechanism and policy must be separable.
findings.proposed_change: Give C-LIFETIME the mechanism only (retirement service, tokens, epochs). Move the policy text to a core-runtime-architect contract section, or make core-runtime-architect the C-LIFETIME owner with concurrency-primitives as implementer. Reduce CORE.OBJ.references to entity-handle semantics that cite the policy.

verdict.reason: C-LIFETIME's summary duplicates the ownership-rules wording of CORE.LIFE.ownership-model owned by another skill, but that capability already says 'policy; retirement service implemented in CORE.CONC.retirement', so the defect is mostly a contract-wording and ownership clarity fix and minor rather than major.

findings.finding: C-CRASH says its handler uses PAL process/pipe primitives via C-BASE only. C-BASE contains only the raw page allocator, raw sink, monotonic clock, raw threads and hook tables. Pipes and process spawn are PLAT.PAL.process, part of C-PAL together with the HTTP/TLS client. The async-signal-safe crash path either depends on the full PAL or has no defined primitive.
findings.evidence: Breakpad/Crashpad out-of-process designs need pre-opened fds/pipes, raw write, an alternate stack and an exception-port hook that exist before any layered init.
findings.proposed_change: Add a signal-safe subset to C-BASE: pre-opened fd/pipe write, raw file write, alternate-stack reservation, exception/signal handler registration hook, monitor-process spawn. Keep PAL.process for the rest. Align C-CRASH summary and requires, and add a C-BASE conformance case for the crash path with no C-PAL initialized.

verdict.reason: C-CRASH requires only C-BASE and C-INSTR yet says it uses PAL process and pipe primitives that are in C-PAL rather than C-BASE; the async-signal-safe path has no defined pre-init primitive, so the C-BASE subset proposal is sound.

findings.finding: Contract requires understate real dependencies, and milestone freeze ordering is proved only against requires. C-CFG requires only C-BASE though typed cvars, strings and snapshots need C-TYPES/C-MEM. C-MEM omits C-LIFETIME although arena reset is keyed to it. C-RES omits C-FRAME though it drains residency at a declared frame phase. C-GPUMEM obeys pool hooks declared in C-RES without either requires or a stated inversion.
findings.evidence: The rule that a freeze never precedes its requirements is only as strong as the requires data. Skill-level consumes already list C-LIFETIME and C-FRAME for these owners.
findings.proposed_change: Add requires C-CFG to C-TYPES (or define a no-allocator C-TYPES subset for pre-C-MEM use), C-MEM to C-LIFETIME, C-RES to C-FRAME. Declare the C-GPUMEM to C-RES hook as an inversion owned by C-RES. Re-run check.py to confirm the SCCs stay acyclic.

verdict.reason: The requires edges are understated (C-CFG to C-TYPES, C-MEM to C-LIFETIME, C-RES to C-FRAME) and I confirmed check.py stays at 0 errors with them added, but the fix is a data-only edit and the C-GPUMEM inversion point is thin, so this is minor rather than major.

findings.finding: CORE.JOBS.thread-model claims to be the sole authority on which threads exist, but CORE.FRAME.pipelining decides by ADR whether a dedicated render/RHI thread exists, and audio, IO and network owners create their own threads. Oversubscription detection has no complete inventory.
findings.evidence: AAA engines (Frostbite, Destiny, UE) keep one central thread and priority table. Per-subsystem ad-hoc threads oversubscribe hybrid-core and 4-core devices.
findings.proposed_change: Reword FRAME.pipelining so the ADR fixes pipeline depth and lane roles while thread-model registers the resulting threads. Require all skills to obtain threads or lanes only through the thread-model inventory, enforced by a lint, with real-time lanes named.

verdict.reason: CORE.JOBS.thread-model claims sole authority on threads while CORE.FRAME.pipelining decides by ADR whether a render/RHI thread exists, a real boundary conflict correctly rated minor.

findings.finding: No capability owns emulating a lower hardware tier on stronger dev/CI machines (core-count and P/E affinity masks, hard process memory ceiling at the tier budget, IO throttle, GPU clock caps). The scale-down proof is data closure only, and nothing runs the min-spec configuration under real constraints.
findings.evidence: Devkits carry extra RAM compared with retail, hiding OOM. UE and Unity device-profile previews and cgroup-limited CI containers are the usual workaround.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.METH.tier-emulation (owner performance-architect, contributors test-runtime-harness, ci-cd-automation, memory-allocators, async-io-storage), using CORE.MEM.budget-enforcement and a PAL throttle/fault hook, run in a CI lane per configuration and gating C-BUDGET lines.

verdict.reason: No capability covers running a lower tier under real constraints (only budget-enforcement, fault-points, core masks in parallel-scaling, and a render-only scalability preview), though 'QA.HOST' is a prefix not an id; a minor omission with a sound proposal.

findings.finding: No memory-side row states executable-memory policy (W^X, JIT entitlement, code-page allocation, icache flush). GAM.SCR.aot covers JIT constraints for scripts only, while CORE.MEM.virtual lists page size and commit only. Live coding, shader/ML JIT and Wasm runtimes have no single per-platform capability query.
findings.evidence: iOS and consoles forbid JIT without entitlement. macOS hardened runtime requires the JIT entitlement. Windows CFG/ACG restrict dynamic code.
findings.proposed_change: Extend CORE.MEM.virtual or add CORE.MEM.exec-pages with per-platform executable-mapping capability queries from PAL. Have GAM.SCR.aot, XC.ITER.live-coding and XC.SEC.hardening consume it.

verdict.reason: No executable-memory, W^X or JIT-entitlement capability exists; GAM.SCR.aot covers scripts only and CORE.MEM.virtual has only page size and commit, so a single per-platform query is a real minor omission.

findings.finding: The capability carrying the O(changes) extraction stance is worded as the legacy per-object render-proxy mirror ('per-frame mirrored copy of every scene object ... CPU cost O(scene objects)'), contradicting C-RSCENE and C-INSTANCES.
findings.evidence: L14 in legacy-patterns.json; 00-design-principles s6; UE5 GPU Scene dirty-primitive tracking, Unity BatchRendererGroup persistent instance data.
findings.proposed_change: Rename to 'Simulation->render extraction: change-tracked deltas into the persistent instance scene (C-INSTANCES); no per-object proxy mirror; CPU cost O(changes)'; add 'mirror' and 'O(scene objects)' to L14 contradiction_terms.

verdict.reason: RND.ARCH.scene-sync is worded as a per-object mirrored copy with O(scene objects) CPU cost while C-RSCENE and L14 say change-tracked O(changes); the rename is sound, but the proposed 'mirror' contradiction term would be regex-scanned by check.py and self-trigger on C-RSCENE's 'no per-object proxy mirror' and the new wording, so use a narrower term.

findings.finding: UI.FW.architecture specifies per-frame property polling through string-keyed bindings, the stringly/polling UI binding that L35 flags; C-UI and the ui-architect purpose say load-time-resolved, change-notified bindings.
findings.evidence: L35 and L20; UI.FW.logic and CORE.REFL.static-default; UMG polled property bindings are a known performance trap; UI Toolkit runtime binding and Slate attributes are the current stance.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'retained UI with change-notified view models and load-time-resolved bindings; no per-frame polling or string-keyed lookup on runtime paths'; add 'polling' and 'string-keyed' to L35 contradiction_terms.

verdict.reason: UI.FW.architecture literally specifies per-frame polling via string-keyed bindings (L35's detection) against C-UI's load-time-resolved change-notified bindings; the reword is right, but the proposed 'polling' and 'string-keyed' terms would match the replacement text under check.py's regex scan, so they need narrowing.

findings.finding: ED.ARCH.transactions says each undo step stores a full copy of the affected scene or asset state (snapshot undo, L38), contradicting C-EDCMD/C-CMD diff-based apply/invert commands and ED.ARCH.transaction-invariants.
findings.evidence: L38; full copies are infeasible for the 10^6-object worlds of ED.UI.outliner and break journal/merge; Unreal transactions and Unity Undo record deltas.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'command/transaction/undo-redo over C-CMD diff-based commands; editor scopes, selection, journal feed; no whole-state snapshots per step'.

verdict.reason: ED.ARCH.transactions states full-copy undo, contradicting L38, C-CMD and C-EDCMD diff-based commands; the check does not catch it because L38's term is 'snapshot-based undo', and the reword is sound.

findings.finding: C-PHYS says contact events are delivered per body through step-time callbacks so gameplay can modify bodies during the step. This is L36 (per-body sync callbacks and mid-step mutation), contradicts PHY.ARCH.events (batched, mutations deferred) and C-SCRIPT deferred-mutation rule, and undermines C-PHYS's own restore+resimulate conformance.
findings.evidence: L36; Jolt/PhysX use contact-modification callbacks only in narrow thread-safe form with batched contact buffers as default; Rapier/Havok use event queues.
findings.proposed_change: Replace with 'per-step batched contact buffer at a declared C-FRAME phase; mutations only via deferred commands; step-time contact-modification hook only as optional read-mostly extension by ADR'.

verdict.reason: C-PHYS summary does say per-body step-time callbacks with gameplay modifying bodies mid-step, which contradicts PHY.ARCH.events (mutations deferred), L36 and the summary's own restore-and-resimulate conformance.

findings.finding: Flake policy is defined as automatic quarantine plus rerun-based clearing with quarantined tests excluded from gate results, i.e. retry-until-green (L69); for autonomous implementers this lets a red test leave the gate by becoming flaky, contradicting QA.AGENT.test-integrity.
findings.evidence: L69; Google/Meta flaky-test practice separates rerun detection from clearing, requiring root-cause label and expiry; quarantined tests must still count in QA.STRAT.release-criteria.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'flake classification and root-cause policy: reruns only classify; quarantine carries owner, expiry and root-cause; quarantined tests still count in release gates; holdout, conformance and determinism lanes are never quarantinable'.

verdict.reason: QA.STRAT.flaky defines quarantine plus rerun clearing with quarantined tests excluded from gate results, which is L69's retry-until-green and lets an autonomous implementer make a red test leave the gate; QA.AGENT.test-integrity does not cover this.

findings.target: CORE.JOBS.degenerate; RES.MGMT.no-stall; CORE.FRAME.host-loop; PLAT.WEB.runtime; legacy L16/L25
findings.finding: CORE.JOBS.degenerate allows blocking waits on the host thread for IO completion, contradicting RES.MGMT.no-stall (no blocking waits on host/OS-bound threads) and CORE.FRAME.host-loop (non-blocking cooperative step); unimplementable on the web main thread and on display-link/Choreographer loops.
findings.evidence: L16, L25; HTML spec forbids Atomics.wait on the window main thread; OPFS sync handles exist only in workers.
findings.proposed_change: Forbid blocking waits on the host thread; inline mode completes IO by cooperative polling of C-TASK completion tokens between frames; record any dedicated-worker exception in CORE.JOBS.blocking.

verdict.reason: CORE.JOBS.degenerate allows blocking host-thread waits for IO, contradicting RES.MGMT.no-stall and CORE.FRAME.host-loop, and is unimplementable on the web main thread; CORE.JOBS.blocking exists to hold the exception.

findings.finding: PRF.METH.budgets lists 'average frame-time' as a budget line although L70's stance and C-BUDGET require percentile lines (p50/p99/p99.9, hitch length, hitches per hour).
findings.evidence: L70; frame-pacing practice.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'average frame-time' with 'p50/p99/p99.9 frame time, max hitch length, hitches per hour'.

verdict.reason: PRF.METH.budgets lists 'average frame-time' against L70's percentile stance, and L70's regex ('average fps|mean fps') does not match it, so the check misses it; small but real, and minor is right.

findings.target: RND.SHADER.neural; C-SHADER; C-MLGPU; radar entry 'In-shader neural evaluation'
findings.finding: Capability says 'single-vendor cooperative-vector tier; no standalone-dispatch fallback'; C-SHADER says 'mandatory standalone-dispatch fallback through C-MLGPU'; radar says fallback is standalone inference dispatch and cites three vendors' intrinsics. The framework contradicts itself on the fallback that keeps non-ML builds buildable.
findings.evidence: 00-design-principles s7 (gated extension points need fallbacks); DXIL cooperative vectors, VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix/NV cooperative_vector and Metal 4 tensors are multi-vendor.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'in-shader small-network evaluation (matrix/tensor intrinsics tier, multi-backend; mandatory standalone-dispatch fallback via C-MLGPU)'; add a C-SHADER conformance case that fused and standalone outputs agree within ML.RT.validation tolerances.

verdict.reason: RND.SHADER.neural says 'no standalone-dispatch fallback' while the C-SHADER contract and the radar entry require the C-MLGPU standalone fallback; this is a direct self-contradiction on the fallback that keeps non-ML builds buildable.

findings.finding: Four skills own an apply/invert, undo/history, journal substrate under different names; C-EDCMD repeats C-CMD's content although it requires it, C-EDIT adds its own undo, and GAM.FW.turns has an undo/history/command-log with no edge to C-CMD. C-CMD is owned by a format skill though apply/invert/merge is behavior.
findings.evidence: One-owner rule and 'contract owner vs implementer' pattern; duplicated journals prevent ED.COLLAB.merge and multi-user merge of UGC sessions.
findings.proposed_change: Make C-CMD the only command core, owned by core-runtime-architect or entity-object-model (schema stays with serialization-schema); reduce C-EDCMD to undo scopes, selection, tool registration and cross-process transactions; reword C-EDIT to sessions/permissions/budgets/publish; add C-CMD to gameplay-architect consumes or justify GAM.FW.turns as a separate clone-cheap log.

verdict.reason: CORE.SER.commands (C-CMD) and ED.ARCH.transactions (C-EDCMD) are distinct capabilities under a deliberate contract-owner versus implementer split and C-EDCMD and C-EDIT already require C-CMD, so the real residue is duplicated summary prose and a missing GAM.FW.turns edge, not a major one-owner violation; moving C-CMD ownership is a preference.

findings.target: contracts.json oracle_author: functional-automation-soak (34 contracts), simulation-validation (28), render-validation (24), robustness-fuzzing (19), foundation-conformance (7)
findings.finding: Oracle authorship is concentrated in four generalist skills lacking the contracts' expertise: functional-automation-soak authors conformance for C-IO, C-BUILD, C-PKG, C-EDCMD, C-GRAPH, C-CMD, C-STATECLASS, C-VFX; robustness-fuzzing authors semantic conformance for C-PAL, C-MOD, C-ID, C-REFL, C-SER, C-FRAME, C-FLOW, C-PRESENT while foundation-conformance (created for foundation contracts) owns only 7. 34 suites in one agent is a bottleneck for the oracle-independence rule.
findings.evidence: oracle_author counts computed from contracts.json; conformance ownership in seL4/Chromium/Linux is per subsystem, not per test technique.
findings.proposed_change: Move L0-L2 foundation contracts (C-PAL, C-MOD, C-SYNC, C-TASK, C-LIFETIME, C-ID, C-REFL, C-SER, C-FRAME, C-FLOW, C-PRESENT, C-IPC) to foundation-conformance; add experts tools-pipeline-conformance (C-COOK, C-BUILD, C-PKG, C-EDCMD, C-GRAPH, C-CMD, C-IMPORT, C-VCS, C-EDVIEW, C-EDHOST, C-EDPREVIEW, C-TARGETPLAT) and content-runtime-conformance (C-IO, C-VFS, C-ASSET, C-RES, C-SAVE, C-GAMEDATA, C-STATECLASS); add a check capping contracts per oracle author (~20).

verdict.reason: Counts are correct (34/28/24/19/7) and concentration with foundation-conformance underused is real, but check.py already proves independence per tier and the concern is a workload and expertise smell, so major is inflated (minor or moderate); the cap check is sound but adding two expert skills is heavy.

findings.target: QA.CONF.memory-model; QA.CONF.foundation; C-SYNC/C-LIFETIME/C-TASK oracle_author; CORE.CONC.correctness; QA.ROBUST.concurrency
findings.finding: Memory-model litmus and model-checking suites are owned by foundation-conformance (QA.CONF.memory-model) while the oracle_author of C-SYNC, C-LIFETIME and C-TASK is robustness-fuzzing, and CORE.CONC.correctness delegates suite authorship to the oracle_author; two skills own the same suites and non-responsibility lists do not resolve it.
findings.evidence: Memory-model verification uses model checking/litmus tools (CDSChecker, Relacy, loom, herd7), a different technique from schedule-perturbation stress.
findings.proposed_change: Set oracle_author of C-SYNC and C-LIFETIME to foundation-conformance; keep QA.ROBUST.concurrency (stress/perturbation) with robustness-fuzzing; state the split in both purposes.

verdict.reason: QA.CONF.memory-model (foundation-conformance) covers litmus and model-checking lanes for foundation contracts, C-SYNC's oracle_reference names herd7/loom/CDSChecker, yet its oracle_author (like C-LIFETIME's and C-TASK's) is robustness-fuzzing, giving two owners for the same suites; the split proposed is technically sound.

findings.finding: Runtime UGC graph compilation in client targets shares the C-GRAPH node/pin schema, but C-GRAPH is layer 5 tool-only and C-EDIT (L4) does not formally require it; the prose bypasses the rule that runtime code may not consume tool contracts, so clients must either pull in the editor graph framework or duplicate the schema.
findings.evidence: Layering rule (L5 only via tool_consumes); check.py sees only listed consumes/requires, not summary prose.
findings.proposed_change: Add a runtime contract (e.g. C-GRAPHRT, L2/L3, owned by graph-editor-framework or scripting-runtime) for node/pin schema, validation and restricted node-set profile; C-GRAPH consumes it tool-side, C-EDIT requires it; remove the prose sharing.

verdict.reason: C-EDIT (L4) and XC.EXT.runtime-graphs cite C-GRAPH (L5 tool-only) as shared schema in prose, but C-EDIT requires and modding-ugc consumes only C-CMD and C-EDCMD via tool_consumes, and no runtime graph contract exists, so the layering rule is bypassed unseen by check.py.

findings.target: GAM.DATA.surface-types; C-GAMEDATA; C-ENV; C-PHYS; C-AUDIO; C-VFX; C-MATIF; physics-architect, terrain, audio-content-runtime, vfx-particles, material-system
findings.finding: The surface-type taxonomy shared by physics, terrain, audio, VFX, decals, projectiles and haptics is owned by a gameplay-layer data skill, and none of the consuming skills consumes C-GAMEDATA nor do their contracts require it; the most widely shared identifier space has no dependency edge (physics-2d in min2d depends on IDs from a skill it does not consume).
findings.evidence: C-GAMEDATA summary and PHY.ARCH.materials; UE physical materials/surface types and Unity PhysicMaterial with FMOD/Wwise surface switches use a registry below gameplay.
findings.proposed_change: Create a small L2 taxonomy contract (owner entity-object-model or content-pipeline-architect, format via C-ASSET) or move the capability under C-ASSET; add consumes edges from the five skills and make C-GAMEDATA a client.

verdict.reason: GAM.DATA.surface-types is owned by gameplay-data, PHY.ARCH.materials and C-GAMEDATA reference it across domains, yet physics-architect, terrain, audio-content-runtime, vfx-particles and material-system have no C-GAMEDATA consume edge; a low-layer shared taxonomy contract is the sound fix.

findings.target: organizations.json; ARCH.ORG.staffing; ARCH.ORG.delegated-planning; radar entry 'Coordination of ~150 autonomous agents'
findings.finding: The program targets ~150 agents (156 skills) but the largest staffing tier is 16 agents each hosting a whole workstream (rendering 26 skills, foundation 20, simulation 18); no tier exists at skill or lead-subtree granularity, so ledger locks, write sets and independence are never proven at the intended scale, and intra-workstream independence cannot be checked.
findings.evidence: organizations.json tiers; independence proof runs only per workstream grouping; single 'quality' agent authors all oracles (see K-ARCH-10).
findings.proposed_change: Add an 'xl' tier (one agent per skill or per lead subtree for leads with >10 children) with the same independence proofs, and encode the promised co-hosting cap (capabilities/contracts per agent) in data and check.py.

verdict.reason: The largest tier is 16 agents and the co-hosting cap promised in ARCH.ORG.independence is not enforced in check.py, but independence pairs and oracle authors are already proven never to share a workstream (so any finer partition preserves them) and the radar records the 150-agent scale as an M entry with a human fallback; only the cap gap is real, so minor.

findings.target: accessibility purpose vs ui-architect, post-color-hdr; UI.A11Y.subtitles, UI.FW.subtitles, RND.POST.colorblind, UI.FW.text-scale
findings.finding: accessibility's purpose claims to own subtitles/captions, colorblind and contrast modes and text scaling, while its non-responsibilities and the capability owners assign subtitle presentation and text scaling to ui-architect and colorblind passes to post-color-hdr; a generated SKILL.md would claim files the ledger assigns elsewhere.
findings.evidence: Framework's own 'policy vs implementation' pattern; capability owners in capabilities.json.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite purpose: defines requirement mapping, services (C-A11YRT), settings and validation; presentation owned by ui-architect, post-color-hdr, input-system.

verdict.reason: accessibility's purpose claims subtitles, colorblind modes and text scaling while its own non-responsibilities assign subtitle presentation to ui-architect and colorblind passes to post-color-hdr, so a generated SKILL.md would claim territory the ledger assigns elsewhere; a small purpose rewrite fixes it.

findings.target: purposes of modding-ugc, spatial-transforms, visual-debugging-tools, serialization-schema, reflection-metadata, core-runtime-architect, platform-architect, net-session, physics-architect, world-architect
findings.finding: Purposes omit contracts the skill provides: modding-ugc provides only C-EDIT but its purpose lacks in-game creation, runtime graphs and distribution integrity; spatial-transforms omits the C-VIEW view registry; visual-debugging-tools omits C-AUTOMATION; also C-CMD, C-STATECLASS, C-IPC, C-BASE/C-TARGETPLAT, C-HOSTAUTH, C-CHARCTRL, C-ENV.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md is generated from purpose+capabilities+contracts; leads must own their contract in prose.
findings.proposed_change: Add one clause per provided contract to each purpose; split mod platform from in-game creation only if modding-ugc exceeds the capability cap.

verdict.reason: The purposes do omit provided contracts (modding-ugc, spatial-transforms, visual-debugging-tools and others), but SKILL.md generation also lists capabilities and contracts and check.py already requires leads to own a contract, so this is completeness polish rather than a material defect.

findings.target: C-GPUMEM->C-RES; C-RSCENE->C-INSTANCES; C-SEQ->C-FLOW; C-AI/C-AIAGENT->C-REPLAY; C-SNAPSHOT/C-SRVDATA->C-STATECLASS; C-EDIT->C-SER/C-ID/C-FRAME; C-INTEGRITY->C-ID/C-FRAME; C-ASSET/C-PHYS/C-ANIM/C-AUDIO->C-ID
findings.finding: Contract summaries or requires name dependencies that the owner skill's consumes list lacks, so the closure proof (which runs on consumes) never sees them (e.g. gpu-memory-resources consumes only C-RHI/C-GPUTIER/C-LIFETIME though residency obeys the C-RES arbiter; C-RSCENE names C-INSTANCES without requiring it).
findings.evidence: Comparison of contracts.json requires and summary references against skills.json consumes for each owner.
findings.proposed_change: Add the edges to requires and consumes (optional where gated); add a check that every C-X in a summary is in requires or an explicit informs list and every owner consumes what its provided contracts require.

verdict.reason: Comparing data confirms summary references and requires missing from owner consumes (C-GPUMEM to C-RES, C-RSCENE to C-INSTANCES, C-SEQ to C-FLOW, C-AIAGENT to C-REPLAY and others), so closure proofs cannot see them; some are downstream mentions or implicit universals, so the proposed lint needs an informs list, but the minor rating is fair.

findings.target: input-system, xr-runtime, online-services-liveops (parent platform-architect); C-SERVER vs C-HOSTAUTH
findings.finding: input-system couples to gameplay and UI but sits under platform-architect; xr-runtime is mostly render-side; online-services-liveops has 4 of 5 consumers in the online workstream, so their disputes always escalate to the root. C-SERVER repeats budgets/overload/kick-ban clauses that C-HOSTAUTH owns, and the name C-HOSTAUTH suggests auth (NET.SESS.auth).
findings.evidence: Consumer/contributor lists; ARCH.ORG.escalation sends cross-workstream disputes to engine-architect.
findings.proposed_change: Re-parent input-system under ui-architect or gameplay-architect (keep C-DEVICE in platform), online-services-liveops under network-architect (keep C-SVC in platform), xr-runtime under render-architect/gpu-platform-architect; rename C-HOSTAUTH to C-HOSTCTL and drop the duplicate clause from C-SERVER.

verdict.reason: C-SERVER does repeat clauses that C-HOSTAUTH owns, but re-parenting three skills and renaming a contract are org-taste judgments without demonstrated breakage, and the escalation argument is unevidenced; only the small C-SERVER duplicate-clause cleanup is defensible.

findings.target: RND.GI.restir (E); RND.LIGHT.stochastic (M); RND.PT.realtime (M); NET.TRANS.web (E) vs NET.TRANS.quic (M)
findings.finding: ReSTIR GI is labelled established while ReSTIR DI and real-time path tracing (whose radar tech name is the same 'ReSTIR GI & path-traced GI') are emerging; NET.TRANS.web (E) prefers WebTransport datagrams while NET.TRANS.quic (M) treats QUIC/WebTransport as emerging.
findings.evidence: Ouyang et al. 2021 (ReSTIR GI), Lin et al. 2022 (ReSTIR PT); WebTransport is not yet in every browser engine.
findings.proposed_change: RND.GI.restir -> M with radar entry (fallback RND.GI.hybrid); NET.TRANS.web -> 'WebRTC unreliable channels (E) preferred; WebTransport (M via NET.TRANS.quic) when available'.

verdict.reason: RND.GI.restir is E while RND.LIGHT.stochastic and RND.PT.realtime are M under the same ReSTIR lineage (the PT radar entry even reuses the tech name), and NET.TRANS.web (E) prefers WebTransport whose own capability NET.TRANS.quic is M; the internal inconsistency is real and the fix is small and sound.

findings.finding: rhi-d3d12 is tagged platforms ['pc','mobile'] but D3D12 does not exist on iOS/Android; gpu-platform-architect's purpose lists inference infrastructure although ml-inference-runtime sits under core-runtime-architect; the design doc states 123 experts / 23 process skills while skills.json has 126 / 26.
findings.evidence: skills.json platforms and tier/kind counts; 00-design-principles s8 boundary table.
findings.proposed_change: rhi-d3d12 platforms ['pc'] (console D3D12-class via rhi-console); drop 'inference' from gpu-platform-architect purpose or re-parent ml-inference-runtime; regenerate the counts in sections 1-2 from data.

verdict.reason: rhi-d3d12 is tagged pc and mobile (D3D12 not on iOS/Android; rhi-vulkan and rhi-metal cover mobile), gpu-platform-architect's purpose lists inference infrastructure though ml-inference-runtime is under core-runtime-architect, and the doc's 123 experts and 23 process skills disagree with the data's 126 and 26; all minor doc and data hygiene.

findings.finding: The C-PHYS summary says contact events are delivered through step-time callbacks so gameplay can react and modify bodies during the step. Legacy L36 and PHY.ARCH.events say the opposite (no mid-step world mutation, mutations deferred). An implementer can follow the contract and build the banned pattern. With parallel islands the callbacks run in nondeterministic order, which breaks the determinism level and the restore-and-resimulate conformance.
findings.evidence: Jolt ContactListener and PhysX contact modification only adjust contact settings or reject contacts, must be thread-safe, and may not add or remove bodies. Box2D v3 returns events after the step.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite the C-PHYS clause: step-time callbacks are contact-modification only and pure. Body mutation goes through the deferred command buffer at a named sync point. Reactive events are batched after the step and sorted by canonical body ID above determinism level none. Cite the split in L36 stance_capabilities.

verdict.reason: C-PHYS summary says contact events use step-time callbacks so gameplay can modify bodies during the step, which directly contradicts L36 (default stance: deferred commands, no mid-step mutation) and PHY.ARCH.events (mutations deferred); the split proposal is technically sound.

findings.target: NET.SRV.zoning, NET.SRV.cross-server, C-SHARD, physics-architect, vehicle-physics, character-physics
findings.finding: No physics skill consumes C-SHARD or contributes to NET.SRV.zoning or NET.SRV.cross-server. Nothing owns live-body authority transfer (velocity, sleep, joints, passengers), bodies straddling a server boundary, ghost-body collision against neighbour-owned bodies, or vehicles crossing boundaries. PHY.ARCH.persistence covers only cell dehydrate and rehydrate.
findings.evidence: Star Citizen server meshing and SpatialOS boundary physics are the known hard problem; Sea of Thieves avoids it by sharding whole ships. The persistent-world profile is claimed by the AAA server configuration.
findings.proposed_change: Add PHY.ARCH.migration (live body, joint-graph and controller hand-off across authority boundaries; ghost-body policy; declared unsupported cases) owned by physics-architect with server-scaleout-persistence and replication. Add C-SHARD? to consumes of physics-architect, vehicle-physics and character-physics. Add physics-architect as a contributor to NET.SRV.cross-server. Add a physics hand-off record to C-SHARD.

verdict.reason: No physics skill consumes C-SHARD and no capability owns live body, joint or vehicle hand-off across server boundaries (PHY.ARCH.persistence covers only dehydrate/rehydrate), but A5 records meshing as M/X with zoning as fallback, so ghost-body parts are experimental and the gap is moderate rather than major.

findings.target: ANM.IK.physical, PHY.TOOL.physics-asset, GAM.MOVE.transitions, C-MOVE, C-CHARCTRL, C-ANIM
findings.finding: The capsule to ragdoll to get-up transition has no owner across character-physics, ik-procedural-animation and character-movement. GAM.MOVE.transitions covers only mount and vehicle, and C-MOVE has no ragdoll state. Ragdoll authority class (cosmetic, replicated or restorable), ragdoll LOD and budget, and pose hand-back to the animation graph are unowned. NET.REP.physics-bodies covers single bodies, not articulated pose.
findings.evidence: Death and hit-reaction ragdolls appear in most action games. The kinematic-to-simulated switch is a known popping and desync source (UE Chaos ragdoll replication). Whether ragdoll is cosmetic decides whether it sits outside C-SNAPSHOT.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.MOVE.ragdoll-transition (owner character-movement, with ik-procedural-animation and character-physics) covering the state machine, capsule and body-set handover, and authority class (cosmetic by default). Add a ragdoll body budget to PHY.ARCH.budget-degradation. Add a ragdoll hand-back clause to C-ANIM.

verdict.reason: GAM.MOVE.transitions covers only mount/vehicle, C-MOVE has no ragdoll state, and ANM.IK.physical/PHY.TOOL.physics-asset cover blending and authoring only, so the capsule-to-ragdoll-to-get-up handover and its authority class are genuinely unowned.

findings.finding: C-PHYS needs an implementer and lists rigid-body-dynamics and physics-2d. Half its surface (batched queries, filtering, shapes, collider history) is owned by collision-detection, which has implements: []. Rigid-body-dynamics implements the contract but owns no query capability, so an implemented check passes while queries and shapes have no explicit implementer.
findings.evidence: In Jolt, PhysX and Bullet the collision and query module is separate and unified behind a world facade. The framework's own principle separates contract owner from implementer.
findings.proposed_change: Set collision-detection implements [C-PHYS] and split the C-PHYS text: rigid-body-dynamics implements bodies, stepping and snapshot; collision-detection implements shapes, queries and collider history. Alternatively add a C-COLLIDE sub-contract.

verdict.reason: collision-detection owns PHY.COL.queries/shapes/filtering yet implements [] while rigid-body-dynamics implements C-PHYS with no query capability, so the implementer mapping is real but it is a labeling clarification of a middleware-facade contract, i.e. minor not major.

findings.finding: Client-side presentation of replicated bodies has two owners. NET.REP.physics-bodies lists prop extrapolation; NET.PRED.physics lists interpolation, extrapolation and smoothing. Nobody owns correction and snap policy.
findings.evidence: In Rocket League-style networked physics, extrapolation and smoothing is a single policy. Two owners would write competing client-side views.
findings.proposed_change: NET.PRED.physics owns all client-side presentation of replicated bodies (extrapolation, smoothing, snap thresholds). NET.REP.physics-bodies is limited to wire content, priority and ownership hand-off. State this in both non-responsibilities.

verdict.reason: NET.REP.physics-bodies lists prop extrapolation while NET.PRED.physics lists interpolation, extrapolation and smoothing, with no owner for snap/correction policy; single-owner fix is sound and minor.

findings.finding: These are labelled E with no dimension split, while gap A4 says cross-platform float determinism has thin evidence. Established evidence covers 2D, fixed-point and same-binary lockstep. General 3D rigid-body lockstep across ISAs is not established. NET.PRED.physics-rollback is correctly M.
findings.evidence: Photon Quantum ships fixed-point physics. Box2D v3 and Jolt document cross-platform determinism only under fixed compiler and flag constraints. Rapier has an enhanced-determinism mode.
findings.proposed_change: Keep 2D and fixed-point at E. Split NET.PRED.physics-lockstep into a 2D or fixed-point E row and a 3D cross-platform-float M row. Add a radar entry with the revisit condition that a shipped title runs 3D rigid-body lockstep across two ISAs.

verdict.reason: Cross-platform float determinism is already an M capability (CORE.MATH.deterministic) with a radar entry citing A4, NET.PRED.physics-lockstep is gated to backends declaring the deterministic level, and fixed-point is the stated fallback, so the proposed new radar entry and row split are largely redundant.

findings.finding: cloth-deformables consumes neither C-SNAPSHOT nor C-STATECLASS, and C-DET only optionally. Ropes and cables are gameplay-visible and can be rollback-relevant, while cloth and hair are cosmetic. Nothing declares the state class per soft-body kind, so conformance cannot say whether a rollback configuration must restore a rope.
findings.evidence: The framework requires every component to have a state class and every snapshot participant to declare cost.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-SNAPSHOT? and C-STATECLASS to cloth-deformables. Declare cloth and hair as derived or cosmetic and excluded from hashes. Declare ropes and softbody as restorable when gameplay-visible. Add ropes to the NET.PRED.physics-rollback conformance list.

verdict.reason: cloth-deformables consumes neither C-SNAPSHOT nor C-STATECLASS (C-STATECLASS is not universal) and C-DET only optionally, so ropes' rollback participation and cloth's cosmetic class are undeclared; minor fix is sound, though the referenced rollback conformance list is not clearly a defined artifact.

findings.target: C-VEHICLE, C-CROWD, C-MOVE, C-CHARCTRL, C-AI, QA.SIM.deformables
findings.finding: The oracle_reference for these contracts is the boilerplate 'reference scenes or analytic cases declared in the conformance suite; derived goldens are regression-only'. It names no independent oracle. C-PHYS names analytic scenes and differential runs.
findings.evidence: Vehicles: Pacejka tire curves, ISO 3888 double lane change, ISO 4138 steady-state circle. Crowds: ORCA/RVO antipodal-circle and bottleneck scenarios. Controllers: analytic slope, step and ledge cases. Deformables: cantilever and pendulum-cloth cases.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the boilerplate in these contracts with the named references. Set the C-PHYS differential reference to a backend other than the shipped one.

verdict.reason: C-VEHICLE, C-CROWD, C-MOVE, C-CHARCTRL and C-AI carry the generic boilerplate oracle_reference (QA.SIM.deformables is a capability, not a contract) while C-PHYS names analytic scenes; naming independent oracles is a sound minor improvement.

findings.target: PHY.FLUID.grid, GAM.SIM.fields, GAM.SIM.cellular, PHY.DYN.buoyancy, C-ENV, water-ocean
findings.finding: Water and fire on a grid can be claimed by four owners: PHY.FLUID.grid, GAM.SIM.fields, GAM.SIM.cellular and the C-ENV water volume from water-ocean or voxel providers. The non-responsibilities differ only by the words continuum and particle. Nothing says which representation is gameplay-authoritative or which may feed the others.
findings.evidence: Noita, Teardown and Oxygen Not Included use cellular or grid authority for gameplay. Niagara Fluids and Flex-class fluids are cosmetic or one-way coupled.
findings.proposed_change: Add a decision table to PHY.FLUID.grid: gameplay-authoritative liquid or fire is cellular (GAM.SIM.cellular or GAM.SIM.fields). PHY.FLUID.* is presentation-grade with one-way coupling into C-PHYS bodies. C-ENV water volume is authoritative for buoyancy.

verdict.reason: PHY.FLUID.grid, GAM.SIM.fields, GAM.SIM.cellular and C-ENV water volume overlap with only a continuum/particle wording split in non-responsibilities and no statement of gameplay-authoritative representation or coupling direction; a decision table is a reasonable minor fix.

findings.finding: C-SHARD defines an entity migration protocol but no participant interface. Only replication consumes it, optionally. Physics, movement, ability/effect, AI and script state have no hand-off hook, so non-replicated simulation state is silently dropped on migration.
findings.evidence: EVE node hand-off, SpatialOS component authority delegation and BigWorld cell migration all use per-component hand-off callbacks. C-NETSESSION and C-SIGNIF already have participant or handler interfaces; C-SHARD has none.
findings.proposed_change: Add on_migrate_out/on_migrate_in/ghost_border participants to C-SHARD. Add consumes edges (C-SHARD@module) to physics-architect, character-movement, gameplay-systems-toolkit and the AI skills. Add a migration state class to C-STATECLASS.

verdict.reason: C-SHARD's summary lists only a migration protocol and authority transfer, no participant hooks, and only replication consumes it (optionally); C-SIGNIF's per-domain handlers cover tier transitions, not cross-server hand-off.

findings.target: dedicated-server, net-session, online-lockstep/online-rollback configurations, NET.PRED.spectator, NET.SESS.host-mode, NET.ARCH.async-validation
findings.finding: No server or headless-client configuration exists for online-lockstep or online-rollback, and dedicated-server (all NET.SRV.*) is gated to profile online only. Relay-hosted rollback, dedicated or tournament lockstep hosts, spectator fan-out and ranked-result validation are never proven buildable. Async validation exists but nothing equivalent exists for lockstep or rollback.
findings.evidence: Age of Empires DE and StarCraft II lockstep relay/host; fighting games use relay-based rollback (Steam Datagram Relay class). Two-peer hash voting cannot validate ranked results (framework A4/L47).
findings.proposed_change: Add online-lockstep and online-rollback to dedicated-server profiles or add a lean command-relay skill. Add configurations rts-2d-lockstep-server and fighting-2d-rollback-relay-server with a headless observer/validator client. Extend NET.ARCH.async-validation to lockstep and rollback replays.

verdict.reason: dedicated-server is profile online only and no server or headless config has online-lockstep or online-rollback profiles, while mobile-async-validator already sets the precedent for a headless validator.

findings.finding: Only relay operation is external. No skill owns the server-side implementation of the relay (a ticket-validating forwarder) or the master/directory server that server-browser and community-hosting presuppose. Platform relays are just C-NETLINK backends, so P2P, rollback and community-hosted play have no self-contained path.
findings.evidence: Valve SDR and master server, Photon/Unity Relay, Nakama are shipped server-side components. L46 relay-shielded addressing is unimplementable without a reference relay.
findings.proposed_change: Add NET.TRANS.relay-service (reference relay and directory, stateless, DoS-hardened) owned by network-transport with contributors dedicated-server and net-session. Build it in a server-host configuration and register its control messages in untrusted-inputs.

verdict.reason: Backend services and relay operation are a recorded scope decision (docs/06 C3, network-transport non-responsibility external:backend, docs/00), and the finding brings no new evidence to reverse it.

findings.target: NET.SRV.community-hosting, PLAT.SRV.host-os, platform-desktop, all server configurations
findings.finding: All server configurations build only for platforms [server-host]. platform-desktop supports the server target but is never a member of a server build, so the redistributable player-hosted server build (typically run on Windows PCs) is unproven.
findings.evidence: Valheim, Palworld and Rust community servers ship Windows builds; SteamCMD serves both platforms.
findings.proposed_change: Add a community-server-pc configuration (online + ugc, target server, platforms [pc, server-host]) or extend the platforms of indie-2d-online-moddable-server, and claim it at M4.

verdict.reason: Every server config uses platforms [server-host] only, so a Windows-hosted community server build is unproven, but listen-host configs partly cover player hosting, so this is minor rather than major.

findings.target: C-REWIND, C-PHYS, C-ANIM, PHY.ARCH.rewind, NET.PRED.rewound-world-query, physics-2d, character-movement, vehicle-physics
findings.finding: Collider history is defined in C-PHYS and PHY.ARCH.rewind, pose history in C-ANIM, and both again as providers in C-REWIND. Only rigid-body-dynamics, animation-runtime and gameplay-systems-toolkit consume C-REWIND, all optionally. physics-2d, character-movement (capsules) and vehicle-physics do not. Nothing proves a lag-compensation configuration contains a provider for the volumes it rewinds; 2D online has no provider.
findings.evidence: Source Multiplayer Networking lag compensation rewinds hit volumes and pose; Overwatch GDC 2017 rewinds hitboxes per tick; the capsule is the commonest rewound volume.
findings.proposed_change: Make C-REWIND the single definition and have C-PHYS/C-ANIM refer to it. Add C-REWIND consumption to physics-2d, character-movement and vehicle-physics. Mark C-REWIND needs_implementer wherever NET.PRED.lagcomp is in the configuration, so closure proves a provider.

verdict.reason: The duplicated definition is real, but C-PHYS already carries collider history and is needs_implementer, and prediction-rollback assembles C-REWIND from C-PHYS. The proposed physics-2d-to-C-REWIND edges would run against that layering, and needs_implementer has no per-capability condition.

findings.finding: Shared or client-owned authority is what L43 lists as legacy, yet it is registered E with only replication as contributor, no anti-cheat contributor, no eligibility rule, and is absent from L43's stance_capabilities. Client-owned props and vehicles carry the same gap. Client authority could be chosen by habit while the catalogue looks satisfied.
findings.evidence: Unity NGO distributed authority and Photon Fusion Shared mode document weaker cheat resistance and target co-op or low-stakes games. Rust and Fortnite server-validate client-owned vehicles.
findings.proposed_change: Add anti-cheat-integrity and network-architect as contributors. Add the capability to L43 stance_capabilities. Require an ADR with declared trust tier and C-INTEGRITY validators on deltas. Re-label maturity M for competitive use.

verdict.reason: NET.ARCH.distributed-authority has only the replication contributor and is missing from L43's stance_capabilities, but this is a catalogue-wiring gap, not major, and the maturity relabel to M is unsupported.

findings.finding: C-NETSESSION says its participant interface (provide_baseline, on_reconnect) is implemented by determinism-replay, but that skill has no consumes or implements edge to C-NETSESSION. Lockstep and rollback configurations have no replication, so snapshot plus command catch-up baseline has no provider on the contract path. A direct edge from the C-DET/C-SNAPSHOT layers would point upward, so it must be module-level.
findings.evidence: contracts.json C-NETSESSION versus skills.json determinism-replay consumes [C-MATH, C-TASK, C-SER@C-SNAPSHOT, C-FRAME@C-SNAPSHOT]. Late-join in lockstep needs a snapshot provider (StarCraft II, Factorio).
findings.proposed_change: Add C-NETSESSION@C-REPLAY to determinism-replay consumes, or move the participant role to prediction-rollback and fix the C-NETSESSION text.

verdict.reason: C-NETSESSION's text names determinism-replay as a participant but it has no edge, and a module-level C-NETSESSION@C-REPLAY edge is the right fix. Prediction-rollback already consumes C-NETSESSION and C-SNAPSHOT, so a provider exists on the contract path and this is minor.

findings.target: NET.TRANS.web, network-transport profiles, mobile-async-client, mobile-async-validator, NET.ARCH.async
findings.finding: NET.TRANS.web names WebSocket as the fallback for async or turn-based play, but network-transport is not in the online-async profile, so the async configurations do not contain it. The async channel to the backend (HTTPS/WebSocket, auth, versioning) is not owned in the configurations that need it.
findings.evidence: Profile gating in skills.json; the capability carries no profile tag.
findings.proposed_change: Add online-async to network-transport profiles (reduced module), or move the async clause to NET.ARCH.async under online-services-liveops and state that the channel is HTTPS via C-PAL.

verdict.reason: network-transport profiles are online, online-lockstep and online-rollback, so async configs lack it while NET.TRANS.web names WebSocket for async play; moving the clause to NET.ARCH.async is a sound minor fix.

findings.finding: The E-labelled NET.TRANS.web prefers WebTransport datagrams while the radar and NET.TRANS.quic class QUIC/WebTransport as emerging, so an established row depends on an emerging technology without an M fallback.
findings.evidence: WebTransport has a short cross-browser production record; WebRTC unreliable DataChannels are the established web game path.
findings.proposed_change: Split the row: WebRTC unreliable and WebSocket stay E; move the WebTransport preference to NET.TRANS.quic (M) with the radar fallback.

verdict.reason: The NET.TRANS.web row already lists WebRTC unreliable channels and WebSocket alongside WebTransport, so a fallback exists inside the row and the claim of no fallback is wrong.

findings.finding: Gap analysis A5 says meshing is emerging (M) in data and radar, but data and radar say X.
findings.evidence: capabilities.json and radar.json class X.
findings.proposed_change: Correct A5 to X, or change the data if M is intended.

verdict.reason: docs/06 A5 says emerging (M) in data and radar while capabilities.json and radar.json class NET.ARCH.meshing as X, a real documentation contradiction that is minor.

findings.target: NET.ARCH.versioning, NET.SESS.handshake, NET.TRANS.dos, NET.TRANS.crypto, NET.REP.compat, NET.SESS.auth
findings.finding: Handshake appears in five rows across three owners. The pre-auth sequence (challenge, crypto, auth ticket, version window, layout negotiation) has no single owner of its order or state machine.
findings.evidence: QUIC/DTLS cookie then application handshake layering; ordering errors cause amplification and pre-auth resource exhaustion.
findings.proposed_change: Give the composite connect state machine to NET.SESS.handshake and declare the other rows as steps. Add a C-NETSESSION conformance case that no per-connection state is allocated before the challenge passes.

verdict.reason: Handshake, challenge, crypto, version and layout negotiation are spread over versioning, handshake, dos, crypto, compat and auth rows with no single ordering owner, and the pre-auth ordering conformance case is a sound minor addition.

findings.finding: NET.SESS.host-mode's name includes host migration, which NET.SESS.host-migration also owns.
findings.evidence: capabilities.json rows.
findings.proposed_change: Remove '& host migration' from NET.SESS.host-mode.

verdict.reason: NET.SESS.host-mode's name includes host migration, which NET.SESS.host-migration separately owns, so the name-only overlap is a trivial minor fix.

findings.finding: Hardware tiers define only server instance classes. Network budgets have no client link classes (cellular/metered, broadband, console) or listen-host uplink share, and are not tied to the link-trace corpus per configuration.
findings.evidence: Overwatch GDC 2017 bandwidth practice; home upload bounds a listen host in coop-3d-listen-client; mobile radio-wake cost and data caps; console cert bandwidth and NAT rules.
findings.proposed_change: Extend NET.ARCH.budgets to per-configuration budgets per link class (down, up, host uplink share, radio wake cost) keyed to NET.TRANS.simulation trace classes and checked by PRF.NET.bandwidth.

verdict.reason: Hardware tiers define only server instance classes and NET.ARCH.budgets has no client link classes or listen-host uplink share, so the minor extension keyed to NET.TRANS.simulation traces and PRF.NET.bandwidth is sound.

findings.finding: Online client and server configurations are not paired. The web client lacks ugc while its matching server has it, so content-set agreement is not exercised; the lite mobile open-world online client has no server counterpart; sandbox-online-server has no client configuration.
findings.evidence: configurations in skills.json.
findings.proposed_change: Add a pairs_with field to configurations, add a sandbox-online client, and make check.py require every online client to name a claimed server.

verdict.reason: The unpaired configs exist, but membership means may-be-built (docs/06 C4), the finding gives no failure mode, and a mandatory pairs_with rule would over-constrain existing client-only configs, so this is process preference.

findings.finding: Probe replies from regions, data centres and relays are spoofable UDP data that steer matchmaking region choice, but are not a registered untrusted input, unlike lan-discovery and server-list-entries.
findings.evidence: Registry has lan-discovery, server-list-entries and packets but no probe replies.
findings.proposed_change: Register qos-probe-replies with validating owner network-transport, size/rate/signature limits and a fuzz harness.

verdict.reason: The registry lists lan-discovery and server-list-entries but no probe replies, while NET.TRANS.qos-probe consumes spoofable UDP replies that steer region choice, so a minor registration is warranted.

findings.finding: NET.PRED.lagcomp has no contributors although the rewind cap, hit-registration policy and validation behind L43's 'bounded-rewind validation' span anti-cheat-integrity, gameplay-systems-toolkit and physics-architect. The maximum rewind window is not a declared budget.
findings.evidence: Valve caps rewind (sv_maxunlag); Overwatch and CS2 bound and audit rewind.
findings.proposed_change: Add the three contributors and state the maximum rewind window as a budget in NET.ARCH.budgets.

verdict.reason: NET.PRED.lagcomp has no contributors and no rewind-window budget appears anywhere in data or docs, while L43 stances bounded-rewind validation, so adding contributors and a budget is a sound minor change.

findings.target: C-EDCMD, C-EDHOST, C-GRAPH, editor-architect, milestones M0/M1/M2, C-SER, C-REFL, C-WORLD, C-ECS
findings.finding: Editor contracts are drafted and frozen only at M2 (C-EDVIEW, C-GRAPH and C-VCS freeze at M3), yet about 30 M0/M1 skills (material-system, render-2d-vector, animation-graphs, cinematics-sequencer, world-data-model, gameplay-data, narrative-dialogue, procedural-generation, ui-architect, vfx-particles and others) already carry tool_consumes of them. The data contracts the editor depends on (C-SER, C-REFL, C-WORLD, C-ECS, C-ASSET, C-IMPORT) freeze at M1 with no editor consumer having exercised them. Editor-driven requirements (property-level change journal, stable ids, prefab/override layering, diffable canonical form, undo scopes) surface only after the freezes.
findings.evidence: Every shipped engine retrofitted these late at high cost (Unity SerializedObject/undo layering, UE transaction and One-File-Per-Actor changes). M1 exit is playable reference games with no authoring path other than hand-edited data.
findings.proposed_change: Put editor-architect in M1 and draft C-EDCMD/C-CMD (transactions, journal, selection, headless commandlet authoring loop) at M0/M1. Make editor-architect a mandatory reviewer of the C-SER, C-REFL, C-WORLD, C-ASSET and C-ECS freezes with an 'editor-conformance' freeze criterion (round-trip do/undo/redo over the contract's data). Keep the full GUI editor at M2.

verdict.reason: C-CMD (the diff/journal/merge command core, requires C-SER/C-REFL, property-tested by functional-automation-soak) is already drafted at M0 and C-ECS freezes at M2 not M1, so the claim is partly wrong, and the M2 'indie 2D with tools' placement is the recorded ladder design rather than a proven defect.

findings.finding: The capability text says each undo step stores a full copy of the affected scene or asset state. That is snapshot-based undo, which L38 forbids (default: serializable diff-based commands), and it contradicts C-EDCMD's own summary. check.py only matches the exact phrase 'snapshot-based undo', so this wording evades the contradiction check. Full copies do not scale to 10^6-object worlds, cannot merge across users and cannot feed the recovery journal.
findings.evidence: UE FTransaction stores property-level deltas; Unity Undo.RecordObject snapshots are a known scaling and merge limit; CRDT/OT editing needs operation logs.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'diff/command-based transactions with inverse operations; snapshots only as checkpoints for journal compaction'. Add contradiction_terms 'full copy' and 'stores a copy' to L38.

verdict.reason: ED.ARCH.transactions literally says each undo step stores a full copy of scene/asset state, contradicting L38 and C-EDCMD, and L38's only contradiction term 'snapshot-based undo' does not match it; the rewording and added terms are sound.

findings.target: configurations (tools), voxel-worlds, WLD.TOOL.voxel, fluid-simulation, CNT.IMP.splats, profiles sandbox/hwrt/online-async/experimental
findings.finding: Add-on profiles sandbox, hwrt, online-async and experimental appear in no tools-target configuration. voxel-worlds (sandbox-only) sits in the M2 skill set but in no tools closure, so WLD.TOOL.voxel and the sandbox side of fluid/sim-debug tools are never proven to close with the editor. Experimental tool-side capabilities (splat import and other X rows) and RT-only lighting authoring have no tools configuration; the opt-in path is proven for the client only.
findings.evidence: Sandbox/voxel tooling is a distinct authoring stack (brush editing, pre-generated structures); tool closure differs from client closure.
findings.proposed_change: Add sandbox-2d-tools (min2d+sandbox), rt-required-3d-tools (std3d+hwrt) and aaa-experimental-tools, claimed at M2/M5/M6; add online-async to a tools config or declare it tool-neutral.

verdict.reason: No tools configuration includes sandbox, hwrt, online-async or experimental so voxel-worlds and WLD.TOOL.voxel are never proven closed with the editor, but this is a proof-coverage gap best rated minor rather than major.

findings.finding: No importer capability covers the source formats indie 2D teams author in: layered sprite/animation sources (Aseprite, layered PSD to atlas plus animation tags), sprite sheets, and tile editors (Tiled TMX, LDtk, Ogmo). CNT.IMP.textures lists only EXR/PNG/TIFF/PSD; tilemaps have runtime and painting tools but no import path; 2D skeletal import sits in a runtime skill outside C-IMPORT; font source import and MSDF atlas generation has no cook owner (UI.TXT.fonts is runtime-only). The min2d scale-down path has no route from artist tools into the cook.
findings.evidence: Aseprite, Tiled and LDtk are the de facto 2D indie interchange; Godot, Unity, GameMaker and Defold ship or plug in importers.
findings.proposed_change: Add CNT.IMP.sprites-2d and CNT.IMP.tilemaps under asset-import-interchange (contributors render-2d-vector, physics-2d), route ANM.RT.2d-import through C-IMPORT, and add a font/MSDF import-cook capability (asset-cook-processors with text-fonts contributing).

verdict.reason: No capability covers Aseprite/layered-sprite or Tiled/LDtk import (CNT.IMP.textures lists only EXR/PNG/TIFF/PSD, ANM.RT.2d-import sits in animation-runtime) and font import has no CNT.IMP owner, a real gap for the min2d indie bar.

findings.target: NET domain, replication, net-session, NET.DBG.*, ED.ARCH.pie-net
findings.finding: Networking has no authoring path. There is no *.TOOL capability for replication/relevancy authoring (per-class replication conditions, priority, cull/relevancy, RPC and authority annotations, ownership, rollback window and input-delay tuning). NET.DBG.visualize, NET.DBG.profiler and NET.DBG.session-replay viewers belong to runtime skills whose tool_consumes are empty, so their editor hosting through C-EDHOST/C-EDVIEW is undeclared. The authoring-path check passes only because it is pattern based.
findings.evidence: UE exposes replication settings and Network Profiler in the editor; ECS netcode (ghost authoring) and rollback games need per-component replication authoring and tuning UI.
findings.proposed_change: Add NET.TOOL.replication-authoring and NET.TOOL.net-debug owned by replication (contributors editor-ui-framework, network-transport), validated via CNT.VAL.submit-gate, and give replication/net-session tool_consumes of C-EDCMD/C-EDHOST.

verdict.reason: There is no NET.TOOL capability and replication/net-session have empty tool_consumes (online workstream is outside the authoring check), but CORE.REFL.state-classes already declares replicated properties once and the omission is closer to minor.

findings.finding: ED.ARCH.pie lists only world-editor-viewport as contributor. PIE isolation also depends on input focus/capture and device ownership (input-system), audio focus and mixer isolation (audio-architect), save-profile sandboxing so PIE cannot write real saves (persistence-save), online-service emulation (online-services-liveops PLAT.SVC.emulation), state preservation across reload (hot-reload-iteration) and simulate-vs-play restore (ecs-runtime snapshot). World/physics/frame multi-instance rows exist, but nothing forces these owners to coordinate through the PIE owner's contract.
findings.evidence: Classic PIE bugs: static state surviving sessions (Unity domain-reload off), PIE writing config/saves, audio bleed between PIE and editor previews.
findings.proposed_change: Add contributors input-system, audio-architect, persistence-save, online-services-liveops, ecs-runtime, hot-reload-iteration to ED.ARCH.pie and state PIE-isolation obligations (no process-global state, sandboxed profile, emulated services) in C-EDCMD/C-EDPREVIEW.

verdict.reason: ED.ARCH.pie lists only world-editor-viewport as contributor and the other owners are absent, but this is a contributor-list enrichment on one row (and C-EDPREVIEW is asset-editor preview, not PIE), so it is minor.

findings.finding: C-EDIT is documented as sharing its command schema with C-EDCMD, but C-EDCMD freezes at M2 while C-EDIT drafts at M4 and freezes at M5. The shared schema (permissions, per-creation budgets, replicated edits) freezes before its second consumer exists.
findings.evidence: Freeze rule needs only an owner and one consumer; a shared schema needs both.
findings.proposed_change: Freeze only the editor-specific layer of C-EDCMD at M2 and the shared C-CMD command schema at M5 after a C-EDIT prototype, with a compatibility ADR.

verdict.reason: The shared schema is C-CMD, which C-EDCMD requires and must therefore freeze no later than C-EDCMD, so freezing C-CMD at M5 would violate the never-freeze-before-requirements rule and the proposal is unsound.

findings.finding: The ml profile has no authoring/asset tool path: no importer for model formats (ONNX-class), model-asset inspector, quantization/backend preview, or tolerance-report UI. ml-inference-runtime has no tool_consumes.
findings.evidence: Unity Inference Engine and UE NNE import and inspect ONNX models in-editor.
findings.proposed_change: Add ML.TOOL.model-assets (import, inspect, quantize, per-backend preview) owned by ml-inference-runtime with contributors editor-ui-framework and asset-import-interchange.

verdict.reason: No ML.TOOL or model-import/inspection capability exists and ml-inference-runtime has no tool_consumes; a minor omission for an add-on profile with the proposed owner and contributors plausible.

findings.finding: Live-service content (flags, event schedules, catalog and economy tables, staged rollout) has runtime boundaries but no authoring, validation and publish tool path, and no link to CNT.VAL.submit-gate or ED.COLLAB.review for backend-delivered data.
findings.evidence: Bad remote-config pushes are a common live outage class; live-service studios ship dedicated liveops tooling.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.SVC.liveops-authoring (schema-validated editing, diff, staged publish, rollback) with contributors gameplay-data, editor-ui-framework, content-pipeline-architect.

verdict.reason: online-services-liveops carries an explicit authoring note that live-ops configuration is data through C-GAMEDATA tooling (gameplay-data consumes C-VCS/C-EDCMD, CNT.VAL.submit-gate exists), remote-config changes are on the human-gates register, and backend services are an engine non-goal per docs/06 C3.

findings.finding: Both rows define asynchronous cancellable editor jobs with progress; L37 points only at async-jobs, so ED.ARCH.process carries a duplicate stance outside the legacy check.
findings.evidence: Same owner, same sentence.
findings.proposed_change: Reduce ED.ARCH.process to the in-/out-of-process runtime ADR and crash isolation; leave job semantics to ED.ARCH.async-jobs.

verdict.reason: ED.ARCH.process and ED.ARCH.async-jobs both define async cancellable editor jobs while L37 references only async-jobs, so the duplicated stance is real and the trim is sound.

findings.target: ED.WORLD.blockout, ED.WORLD.mesh-paint, ED.WORLD.gizmos, ED.WORLD.splines, ED.WORLD.color-management, ED.UI.outliner
findings.finding: These 3D-only or large-world editor capabilities carry no profile tags, so minimal-tools and indie-2d-tools inherit 3D manipulation, booleans/UV modeling, mesh painting, HDR preview and the 10^6-object outliner tier.
findings.evidence: Capability-level tags exist for this and are used on ED.WORLD.partitioned; Tiled/LDtk-class 2D tools need none of these.
findings.proposed_change: Tag blockout, mesh-paint, 3D gizmos and splines [lite3d,std3d], color-management [std3d], and the virtualized outliner tier [openworld,team-mid] with a plain tree for small projects.

verdict.reason: The rows are indeed untagged, but tagging gizmos, splines and the outliner away from 2D/small projects would remove needed 2D gizmos, path tools and any outliner from indie configs (C-EDVIEW has a 2D/ortho mode), so the proposal is unsound and the concern is a preference-level scale-down.

findings.target: milestones.json M4 exit / M6 gates; PRF.NET.server-density
findings.finding: M4 exit says server density is gated at M4, but the only gate for PRF.NET.server-density is in M6. Dedicated servers (online-3d-server closes at M4) ship for two milestones with no tick-cost, instances-per-host or cost-per-CCU gate; density is first measured after netcode and replication freezes.
findings.evidence: Tick cost per player and instances per host are architectural (relevancy, per-entity bytes, replication cost) and are expensive to fix after freeze. The exit text and the gate list disagree.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.NET.server-density (validator QA.FUNC.load) as an M4 gate for online-3d-server. Keep any M6 gate as a separate capability or a per-AAA-config gate. Cross-check exit-text perf claims against gates.

verdict.reason: M4 exit text says server density is gated at M4 but PRF.NET.server-density is gated only in M6, and QA.FUNC.load already validates other M4 gates, so moving the gate is sound.

findings.finding: M2 ships mobile-async-client with exit claim 'mobile tier within budget', but the governor and energy/sustained-state gates land in M3. Mobile is judged on footprint, pacing and size only, so cold-burst passes and thermal throttling after minutes is never tested.
findings.evidence: Sustained versus peak throttling is the dominant mobile perf failure (ADPF and iOS thermal-state guidance).
findings.proposed_change: Add an M2 gate for a sustained-state frame-time line on the mobile tier (C-BENCH thermal-soak, validator PRF.BENCH.stats) plus a gate on the mobile thermal-signal backend into the governor. Otherwise defer the mobile within-budget claim to M3.

verdict.reason: M2 gates omit sustained/thermal measurement while governor and energy land in M3, but C-BENCH already specifies thermal-soak, the proposed gate on a governor backend cannot exist before M3 (defer-the-claim is the sound option), and this is a 2D async mobile config, so major is inflated.

findings.finding: All perf gates run on the 'profile' build (shipping optimization with C-INSTR on). Nothing measures the delta to the actual shipping artifact (instrumentation compiled out changes inlining, LTO/PGO, M1-mandated hardening flags, package signature verification, anti-cheat, encryption). Budgets are validated on a binary that never ships.
findings.evidence: Known profile-versus-retail divergence; hardening costs CPU; field telemetry sees it only after release.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.BENCH.shipping-delta (perf-benchmarking; contributors build-system-toolchains, security-engineering): shipping-build smoke benchmark per tier with an overhead line for C-INSTR, hardening and DRM in C-BUDGET, gated at M1 (PC) and M2 (other platforms).

verdict.reason: C-BENCH states gates run on the profile build (BLD.SYS.configs: shipping optimization with C-INSTR), and no capability or gate measures the delta to the actual shipping build with hardening and DRM.

findings.finding: M0 and M1 exits require CI perf lanes and within-budget on min-spec PC, but no gate names the lab, proxy-metrics or lab-scheduling capabilities. The regression gate's validity depends on quiet reference hardware and can be passed on noisy shared runners.
findings.evidence: Chromium and Mozilla perf infrastructure require dedicated labs; rustc-perf uses instruction counts for noise reasons.
findings.proposed_change: Gate PRF.BENCH.proxy-metrics at M0 (validator PRF.BENCH.regression) and PRF.BENCH.lab at M1 (min-spec PC noise qualification), with per-platform lab gates at M2 and M3 for console and mobile devices.

verdict.reason: No milestone gate names PRF.BENCH.lab, proxy-metrics or lab-scheduling although M0/M1 exits depend on CI perf lanes and within-budget on min-spec PC, so regression validity rests on unqualified hardware.

findings.target: M5 gates; xr-*-client configs; C-BUDGET; PLAT.XR.reprojection
findings.finding: M5 claims three XR configurations but its only perf gate is scale-content. C-BUDGET has no XR lines (missed-frame rate, reprojection headroom, compositor deadline margin, motion-to-photon per device) and no perf owner is named for XR pacing.
findings.evidence: OpenXR frame timing and Meta/Valve reprojection guidance; dropped-frame percentage is a certification criterion and a comfort issue.
findings.proposed_change: Add XR lines to C-BUDGET, add an M5 gate for PRF.LOAD.pacing-latency on the XR configurations, and make loading-streaming-performance and the XR platform skill co-own the measurement method.

verdict.reason: M5 claims three XR configs with only PRF.BENCH.scale-content gated, C-BUDGET lines have no XR missed-frame or reprojection lines, and PLAT.XR.reprojection is owned by xr-runtime with no perf co-owner.

findings.finding: These PRF capabilities have no milestone gate at any stage, though they cover the structural bottlenecks (serialization, bandwidth, worst-case sim, cook throughput). The M3 UMA portable console, the CPU-submission and GPU-driven paths, and the M6 distributed cook are claimed with no enforcement of the parallel-efficiency, bandwidth or cook lines.
findings.evidence: C-BUDGET carries a parallel-efficiency-at-N line and a DRAM/fabric bandwidth line that no milestone gate enforces.
findings.proposed_change: Gate PRF.CPU.parallel-scaling and PRF.MEM.bandwidth at M3, PRF.BENCH.sim-worst-case at M5 (validator QA.SIM.mass-agents), and PRF.PIPE.cook and PRF.METH.model at M6.

verdict.reason: PRF.CPU.parallel-scaling, PRF.BENCH.sim-worst-case, PRF.MEM.bandwidth, PRF.METH.model and PRF.PIPE.cook appear in no milestone gate although C-BUDGET carries their lines (gating PRF.METH.model only at M6 is late, but the core omission stands).

findings.finding: Local frame pacing and input-to-photon latency sit under the load/hitch expert, while networked end-to-end latency is a separate row with a different owner and no stated shared budget line, giving a split accounting of one latency chain.
findings.evidence: A latency chain (input, sim, render, present, display, network) must be accounted in one place to avoid double counting in C-BUDGET.
findings.proposed_change: Make PRF.LOAD.pacing-latency the declared local segment consumed by PRF.NET.latency (add loading-streaming-performance as its contributor), or move both to one latency owner.

verdict.reason: C-BUDGET already has a single input-to-photon latency line per refresh class and netcode family, and PRF.NET.latency already lists frame-orchestration as contributor, so the claimed split accounting with no shared line is largely wrong and the fix is cosmetic.

findings.finding: Both labeled E, but PMU access is often unavailable on virtualized CI hosts, GPU counters need admin rights, locked clocks or vendor SDKs on PC and are NDA-gated on consoles. Proxy-metric gating depends on them.
findings.evidence: Cloud VM PMU restrictions; Nsight Perf SDK requirements; GPUPerfAPI licensing.
findings.proposed_change: Relabel the GPU-counter portion as M, keep CPU PMU E on bare-metal lab hosts only, and state a fallback (simulated cache counts on non-PMU hosts).

verdict.reason: Maturity classes describe technique maturity (PMU and vendor GPU counters are established techniques, proxy metrics use instruction counts), while host availability is a platform-access constraint; relabeling to M would require radar entries and misapplies the maturity scheme.

findings.finding: No budget-waiver mechanism exists. C-PERF covers findings and territory loans only, and baseline-governance covers threshold changes. A subsystem over budget on one tier has no recorded waiver-and-recovery path, so agents either block a milestone or quietly relax C-BUDGET.
findings.evidence: Studios track budget debt with named owner and expiry.
findings.proposed_change: Add to C-PERF a budget-waiver record (line, tier, owner, expiry, recovery plan) that the perf gate reads, requiring architect or human signature for waivers that cross a milestone.

verdict.reason: No budget-waiver or budget-debt record exists in C-PERF, C-BUDGET or baseline-governance (which covers threshold changes only), so a per-tier overrun has no recorded owner/expiry path, a modest but real minor contract gap.

findings.target: ARCH.STRUCT.platform-backends, UI.TXT.ime, UI.A11Y.screen-reader, AUD.ARCH.devices, INP.DEV.abstraction, PLAT.DESK.pal, PLAT.MOB.pal, PLAT.WEB.pal
findings.finding: Registered backend slots (audio endpoint, input, sockets, save storage, IME/a11y bridge) have an explicit per-platform implementer only on console (PLAT.CON.confidential-slots). On PC, mobile and web the OS-specific implementations (TSF/IBus/UITextInput/InputConnection/DOM composition; UIA/AT-SPI/UIAccessibility/TalkBack/ARIA; WASAPI/CoreAudio/AAudio; GameInput/evdev/GCController/Gamepad API) sit in platform-neutral domain skills, and the PAL implementation capabilities list only OS services, windowing, threads, clocks, IO, display, power, events. No platform-tagged skill owns them.
