findings.evidence: check.py enforces platform tags only for PLAT.* areas, so this is invisible. Unreal per-platform modules and Unity/SDL platform layers keep these in per-OS layers.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.DESK/MOB/WEB.backend-slots capabilities owned by each platform skill (domain skill = slot-interface owner and contributor); mark the slot contracts needs_implementer so per-platform closure is checked.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: only PLAT.CON.confidential-slots names per-platform slot implementers and the DESK/MOB/WEB PAL capabilities list OS services only, but registered slots are implemented in domain skills (AUD.ARCH.devices, INP.DEV.abstraction, UI.TXT.ime) without a platform-tagged owner, so it is a real ownership gap, though minor-to-major rather than clearly major since domain skills can own their backends and needs_implementer wiring is only partly specified.

findings.target: C-SVC, platform-services, platform-mobile, platform-web, PLAT.SVC.pc-storefronts, PLAT.COMM.iap
findings.finding: C-SVC is not needs_implementer and has no platform list; only platform-console implements it. PC has named adapters, but mobile store/service adapters (StoreKit, Play Billing, Game Center, Play Games, Sign in with Apple) and web-portal SDK adapters are unnamed. Configurations like indie-2d-client (pc, console, mobile, web) close without any mobile or web C-SVC backend.
findings.evidence: Mobile and web ship paths depend on these adapters; PLAT.WEB.audience-share already assumes portal SDKs.
findings.proposed_change: Make C-SVC needs_implementer; add PLAT.MOB.svc-stores (platform-mobile) and PLAT.WEB.svc-portals (platform-web) or per-store variants of platform-services; add a null/emulator implementer per platform.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: C-SVC lacks needs_implementer (only C-PAL, C-RHI, C-PHYS, C-TARGETPLAT, C-CHARCTRL have it), only platform-console implements it, and StoreKit, Play Billing, Game Center and web portal adapters appear nowhere in the data, so indie-2d-client closes with no mobile or web backend; it is real but minor-to-major because platform-services and PLAT.COMM.iap cover store integration in general terms.

findings.target: PLAT.PAL.confidential-extensions, BLD.SYS.platform-sdks, BLD.SYS.toolchains, RND.SHADER.toolchain, ARCH.REQ.hardware-tiers, PLAT.PAL.device-db, C-BUDGET, OBS.CRASH.symbolication, QA.CERT.prechecks, PLAT.CON.submission
findings.finding: NDA handling covers console code and CI results only. Confidential data and process territory is owned by non-NDA skills: console SDK versions and cert-mandated minimums, console compiler matrix, tier records and per-tier budgets with console memory reservations, device-db console SKUs, DDC/cooked console data, symbols/dumps, perf captures. QA.CERT.prechecks (non-NDA) also overlaps PLAT.CON.submission pre-submission checkers.
findings.evidence: check.py CONFIDENTIAL regex matches only 'confidential' or 'console API/SDK'. Console memory reservations, SDK versions and TRC text are NDA-covered while the budget file, register and DDC are readable by all agents.
findings.proposed_change: Add data-class rules to PLAT.PAL.confidential-extensions: per-holder sealed partitions for tier/budget numbers, DDC, symbols, captures with public envelope and sanitized summaries. Split BLD.SYS.platform-sdks into public part plus PLAT.CON.sdk-toolchain (platform-console, NDA). findings.target: skills.json platform-desktop, platform-mobile, platform-web, platform-server-host, platform-console, rhi-d3d12; check.py variant closure
findings.finding: Only RHI backends declare variants; every PAL/C-TARGETPLAT implementer has variants None, which the closure test treats as satisfying every variant, so PAL closure for win-arm64, macos, ios, horizon-os, pico-os, visionos and webkit/gecko is vacuous. platform-desktop spans four OS lineages; the Apple family is split between platform-desktop (macOS) and platform-mobile (iOS/visionOS) though rhi-metal spans all three. rhi-d3d12 is tagged 'mobile' with no mobile variant. findings.evidence: check.py lines 273-278 (null variants = wildcard).

verdict.reason: Confirmed: check.py treats null variants as a wildcard and every PAL/C-TARGETPLAT implementer (platform-desktop, mobile, web, server-host, console) has variants None, rhi-d3d12 is tagged mobile with only pc variants, and console classes bind to no skill, so per-variant PAL closure is vacuous and the proof is weaker than claimed.

findings.finding: Cloud render host (headless GPU render, HW encode, multi-tenant GPU packing) is an implementation capability owned by the lead platform-architect; platform-server-host is defined as 'no display or GPU'; rhi-vulkan has no server-host variant; no configuration or milestone exercises it. verdict.reason: Confirmed: pc variants are win-x64, win-arm64, linux-steamos and macos, server-host variants are Linux only, and no Proton/Wine ADR capability exists (only anti-cheat mentions), so this is a valid minor scale-down gap with an acceptable explicit-non-goal alternative.

findings.target: QA.CERT.licenses, QA.CERT.legal-surfaces, QA.CERT.ratings, QA.CERT.export-crypto, QA.CERT.patents-codecs, QA.CERT.authorship-ip, CNT.ID.rights, ARCH.PROD.licensing-model, ARCH.PROD.upstreaming, ARCH.ORG.human-gates

findings.target: developer-experience-docs, XC.DX.samples, XC.DX.templates, XC.DX.onboarding, XC.DX.creator-docs, XC.DX.doc-tests, ARCH.ORG.human-capacity

findings.target: CORE.MATH.deterministic, PHY.DEST.procedural, NET.PRED.physics-rollback, ANM.SYN.learned, ANM.DEF.ml, GAM.AI.learned, ML.RT.sequence-exec, ML.RT.os-models, RND.SHADER.autodiff, XC.EXT.generated-assets, PLAT.PAL.cloud-render-host, ED.COLLAB.concurrent-world, ARCH.ORG program radar entry
findings.finding: radar.json says M needs two shipped titles with postmortems, but check.py does not enforce it. About a dozen M entries contradict their own evidence or revisit text. CORE.MATH.deterministic evidence says cross-ISA float determinism is not established. PHY.DEST.procedural is called research-grade. NET.PRED.physics-rollback is beta. ANM.SYN.learned cites only Holden 2020. ML.RT.os-models revisit is a shipped title using an OS model API, meaning zero today. RND.SHADER.autodiff evidence is a preview. XC.EXT.generated-assets and GAM.AI.learned have one title each. PLAT.PAL.cloud-render-host needs two first-party hosts. ED.COLLAB.concurrent-world cites non-game evidence. ML.RT.sequence-exec is M while its sibling ML.RT.constrained-decoding is X. X/S rows are opt-in through the experimental profile, while M rows sit in default profiles, so over-labelled rows become silent defaults.
findings.evidence: The framework's own evidence-to-class rule. 2025-26 state: no shipped game consumers of OS model or NPU APIs; cross-ISA float determinism is achieved in production only by fixed-point or same-binary builds.
findings.proposed_change: Reclassify these rows to X and add the experimental profile tag; the fallbacks already exist. Add shipped_titles and postmortems fields to radar entries and make check.py fail an M entry with fewer than two. Add an explicit justified exception field where M is kept for program-level items.

verdict.reason: radar.json _doc states M needs two shipped titles with postmortems and check.py has no such check. The listed M rows contradict their own evidence or revisit text: os-models revisit is a shipped title using an OS model API, GAM.AI.learned cites one title, and ANM.SYN.learned cites only Holden 2020. Reclassifying to X is sound because fallbacks exist, but the ARCH.ORG program entry needs the proposed justified-exception field rather than a flat X.

findings.target: RND.RT.cluster-blas, RND.RT.omm, RND.RT.ser, radar entry Advanced RT hardware features
findings.finding: One M radar entry lumps OMM, SER and cluster BLAS. Its revisit, availability on two or more vendors, is met for OMM and SER (DXR 1.2) but not for cluster acceleration structures, which are NVIDIA-only. By the entry's own trigger cluster-blas is X. The fallback of standard BLAS/TLAS hides that cluster BLAS is what makes virtualized geometry ray-traceable at scale.
findings.evidence: DXR 1.2 spec covers OMM and SER. RTX Mega Geometry / VK_NV_cluster_acceleration_structure is single-vendor (2025).
findings.proposed_change: Split the entry. OMM and SER stay M. Cluster-blas becomes X with the experimental tag, fallback of proxy-mesh BLAS per cluster LOD level (RND.RT.lod), and a trigger of a vendor-neutral D3D12 or Vulkan KHR API.

verdict.reason: The single M entry lumps omm, ser and cluster-blas under a 'two vendors' revisit that cluster-blas does not meet, and RND.RT.lod exists as a fallback target. The three capabilities sit in the opt-in aaa profile, not a default one, so this is a minor labelling split rather than major.

findings.target: NET.TRANS.crypto, XC.SEC.crypto-policy, XC.SEC.pqc-signatures, radar Post-quantum signatures
findings.finding: Post-quantum coverage is signatures only. Harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to key exchange, where hybrid X25519MLKEM768 is already default in browsers and OpenSSL 3.5. Transport and session crypto have no hybrid-KEM or algorithm-agility requirement. ML-KEM adds about 1.2 KB per handshake message, which interacts with NET.TRANS.dos anti-amplification limits and MTU-bounded custom UDP handshakes.
findings.evidence: NIST FIPS 203; IETF draft-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem; QUIC RFC 9000 3x anti-amplification rule.
findings.proposed_change: Rename the radar entry to post-quantum key exchange and signatures. Add NET.TRANS.pq-kex (M, owner network-transport, contributor security-engineering) requiring algorithm ids in handshake formats and a handshake size that fits the anti-amplification budget.

verdict.reason: Only XC.SEC.pqc-signatures exists and no capability or contract mentions KEM or hybrid key exchange. NET.TRANS.crypto is E with no PQ or agility requirement, and anti-amplification is already a NET.TRANS.dos concern, so a minor omission with a sound proposal.

findings.target: radar non-goal GLES/WebGL backends, PLAT.WEB.webgpu-target, configuration indie-2d-online-web-client
findings.finding: Min2d web games require WebGPU. Web 2D is a major indie channel (portals, iframes, playable ads), and WebGPU is gated by browser version, OS, WebViews and iframe policy. The reversal trigger (>10% of audience without WebGPU) is measurable, but reversal would need a whole new C-RHI backend. Nothing reserves a narrow 2D-only presentation sink.
findings.evidence: WebGPU is in all major browsers by 2025-26 but with platform gaps; portal SDKs still ship WebGL2 builds.
findings.proposed_change: Record that any reversal is scoped to a 2D-only sink (batched sprite, tilemap and text draw list, RND.2D.*) behind a C-RENDER2D slot, not a full C-RHI backend. State the slot now so the trigger is actionable.

verdict.reason: No C-RENDER2D slot exists, but the WebGPU-only stance and its measurable reversal trigger are a recorded, reasoned decision in docs/00 and docs/09. Reserving a new contract slot for a hypothetical reversal of a non-goal is speculative and not a defect.

findings.target: radar entries ANM.CINE.timecode, QA.FUNC.agent-exploration, RND.GI.restir vs RND.PT.realtime, memory-safe language x2, work graphs x3, splats x2, WebGPU x2
findings.finding: Radar governance defects. ANM.CINE.timecode has its evidence, revisit and fallback copy-pasted from RND.ARCH.cluster-sync, so the trigger is not a timecode predicate. QA.FUNC.agent-exploration sits under the tech name Agent/automation control API (MCP class). One technology appears as several entries with divergent fallbacks. ReSTIR is class E in one entry and M in another with identical evidence. A milestone-exit review can promote one copy and leave the other stale.
findings.evidence: radar.json entries as listed; the radar-transitions promotion checklist assumes one record per technology.
findings.proposed_change: One radar entry per technology with a capabilities list and a per-capability fallback map. check.py fails duplicate tech names and revisit strings shared across different techs. Give timecode its own predicate, for example a shipped title slaving cinematic playback to external LTC/PTP.

verdict.reason: ANM.CINE.timecode's evidence, revisit and fallback are verbatim copies of RND.ARCH.cluster-sync, so its trigger is not a timecode predicate. The ReSTIR E vs M split with identical evidence is also real, though multi-entry techs are already disambiguated per capability and owner. The merge and duplicate-name check is over-broad, but the timecode defect stands as a minor governance fix.

findings.finding: Sampler-feedback streaming is M inside the default std3d profile, but its evidence is D3D12-only with no cited shipped titles, so it is X by the framework's rule. RND.RECON.upscalers is E as a whole, though DLSS4, FSR4 and PSSR are per-vendor binary ML integrations, unlike the engine-owned temporal upscaler.
findings.evidence: D3D12 sampler feedback has no Vulkan or Metal equivalent. RND.RECON.ml-denoise is already M for the same per-vendor reason.
findings.proposed_change: Move RND.TEX.feedback to X or to the aaa profile. Split RND.RECON.upscalers into E (engine temporal) and M (vendor ML integrations) with fallback engine temporal upscaler.

verdict.reason: RND.TEX.feedback is M in the std3d profile with D3D12-only evidence, no shipped titles and a mip-streaming fallback, so X or aaa is defensible. RND.RECON.upscalers is E as a whole while its sibling ml-denoise is M for the per-vendor reason, so splitting is a sound minor fix.

findings.finding: Stance capability for L14 describes the per-object render proxy mirror (per-frame mirrored copy of every scene object, O(scene objects)), contradicting C-RSCENE and docs/00 s6.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to change-tracked delta extraction into the persistent instance scene, O(changes), no per-object mirror; add contradiction_terms to L14.
findings.evidence: Delta-tracked persistent GPU scenes are O(changes); proxy sync cost scales with object count.

verdict.reason: RND.ARCH.scene-sync literally says per-frame mirrored copy of every scene object, O(scene objects), directly contradicting C-RSCENE's 'no per-object proxy mirror; O(changes)' and L14's stance, and L14 has no contradiction_terms; the reword is sound.

findings.finding: Capability specifies per-frame property polling through string-keyed bindings, the exact L35 legacy; sibling UI.FW.logic says the opposite.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to change-notified view models with bindings resolved at load/compile time; polling only in dev overlays; add terms.
findings.evidence: Change-notified bindings are the modern standard (Unreal MVVM, UI Toolkit runtime bindings, Slint).

verdict.reason: UI.FW.architecture states per-frame property polling through string-keyed bindings, exactly L35's detection, while UI.FW.logic and L35's stance say load-time resolution; L35 has no terms and the fix is sound.

findings.finding: Undo is defined as a full copy of the affected scene or asset state, i.e. snapshot-based undo, unscalable to 10^6-object worlds and unusable as a collaboration journal.
findings.proposed_change: Serializable diff-based commands with inverse ops, journaled for collaboration; add 'full copy of the affected' term.
findings.evidence: Unreal Transactor, Godot UndoRedo, operation-log editors.

verdict.reason: ED.ARCH.transactions says each undo step stores a full copy of the affected state, which is snapshot undo in different words that evades L38's 'snapshot-based undo' term; the diff-command fix is sound.

findings.finding: C-PHYS says contact events are delivered per body via step-time callbacks so gameplay can modify bodies during the step: immediate callbacks and mid-step mutation, contradicting PHY.ARCH.events, async stepping and rollback.
findings.proposed_change: Batched contact/change-set output consumed at a declared point, mutation via deferred command buffers; optional ADR-gated solver-time contact-modification hook only; add terms.
findings.evidence: PhysX/Havok contact-modify listeners serialize the step; Jolt and Rapier use buffered contact lists.

verdict.reason: C-PHYS summary says events are delivered per body via step-time callbacks with gameplay modifying bodies during the step, contradicting PHY.ARCH.events (deferred mutations), L19 and L36; the batched-output fix is sound.

findings.finding: Inline mode permits blocking waits on the host thread for IO completion, contradicting no-stall and being impossible on web main thread.
findings.proposed_change: Limit exemption to headless/tool/pre-first-present contexts; cooperative mode yields to the host event loop with IO completion as continuation.
findings.evidence: WASM main thread cannot Atomics.wait; Android ANR and console watchdogs.

verdict.reason: CORE.JOBS.degenerate allows blocking waits on the host thread for IO completion while RES.MGMT.no-stall forbids blocking host/OS-bound threads, and blocking is infeasible on the web main thread; restricting to headless contexts is sound.

findings.finding: Most patterns (L01-L18, L20-L22, L33, L35 etc.) have no contradiction_terms so check.py cannot catch corrupted stance capabilities; four defects here slipped through.
findings.proposed_change: Add terms: L14 'mirrored copy|proxy mirror|O\(scene objects\)'; L35 'property polling|string-keyed bindings'; L38 'full copy of the affected'; L36/L19 'step-time callbacks|during the step'; L16 'blocking waits on the host'; L02, L03, L21, L33 similar.
findings.evidence: K-LEGACY-1..4 are stance capabilities of L14, L35, L38, L19/L36.

verdict.reason: Only 36 of 88 patterns have contradiction_terms (L14, L35, L36 and L16 have none), which is why K-1 to K-4 escaped, but this is a systemic hardening of a checker rather than a defect in shipped content, and much of its value is delivered once K-1 to K-5 and the proposed terms are applied, so major is slightly high and minor or major-lite fits better.

findings.finding: Rerun-based clearing of quarantined tests is retry-until-green; quarantine has no owner or expiry.
findings.proposed_change: Rerun for classification only; quarantine bounded by owner and expiry; clear after root-cause fix and N clean seeded runs.
findings.evidence: Google/Meta flaky-test practice.

verdict.reason: QA.STRAT.flaky uses automatic quarantine and rerun-based clearing with no owner, expiry or root-cause condition, which matches L69's retry-until-green and evades its term; minor is appropriate.

findings.finding: Budget lines include average frame-time, the legacy metric L70 replaces.
findings.proposed_change: Median plus p99/p99.9 frame time; averages secondary only.
findings.evidence: C-BUDGET already uses p50/p99/p99.9.

verdict.reason: PRF.METH.budgets lists 'average frame-time' lines, the mean-metric legacy L70 replaces, and the term 'average fps' does not match; minor is right.

findings.finding: docs/00 names independent competing streaming pools as replaced legacy but the catalogue has no pattern, owner or check for it.
findings.proposed_change: Add L89 Independent per-domain streaming pools -> single arbitrated budget, owner resource-streaming-architect, stance caps RES.MGMT.arbitration and CORE.MEM.uma, with terms.
findings.evidence: Per-subsystem fixed pools thrash on UMA consoles and Apple silicon.

verdict.reason: docs/00 explicitly lists independent competing streaming pools as replaced legacy, yet no pattern in the catalogue covers it, and RES.MGMT.arbitration and CORE.MEM.uma already carry the stance, so a new L89 is a sound minor addition.

findings.finding: Animation notifies are the classic immediate-callback path and are not a stance capability of L19.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to batched tick-stamped events and add ANM.RT.events to L19 stance_capabilities.
findings.evidence: UE AnimNotify invokes gameplay code from animation evaluation.

verdict.reason: ANM.RT.events is only worded 'Curves, events & notifies' and nothing in the data states an immediate callback, so the defect is speculative inference from UE practice, and adding it to L19 stance_capabilities has no demonstrated contradiction.

findings.target: QA.CERT.privacy, XC.SEC.privacy, NET.SRV.persistence, OBS.CRASH.privacy, OBS.LOG.analytics, XC.DET.replay-format, PLAT.SVC.voice-moderation
findings.finding: Sweep: engineering disciplines and platform/legal. No capability owns executing data-subject rights (access/export, rectification, erasure, portability, retention expiry) across engine-owned personal-data stores. Policy tracking, privacy principles and dump redaction exist, and store-policy lists account deletion as a check, but no mechanism is owned. Missing: a per-user data-class inventory and an erase/export fan-out over server persistence (write-behind, leases, tombstones), telemetry, crash dumps, replays, voice-report captures, UGC and cloud saves, with backup/CDN/DDC propagation and an audit receipt.
findings.evidence: GDPR Arts. 15-20; Apple and Google Play require in-app account deletion; erasure conflicts with write-behind persistence and immutable backups; replays and voice captures contain other players' data. A keyword search of all capability names finds no export/erase mechanism.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.SVC.data-subject-rights (or NET.SRV.data-rights), owner privacy-data-protection, contributors network-architect, crash-diagnostics, observability-telemetry, dedicated-server. Add a C-PRIVACY obligation that every store registering a data class declares export and erase hooks; QA.CERT.privacy verifies it.

verdict.reason: XC.SEC.data-rights already exists (owner privacy-data-protection; contributors certification-compliance, observability-telemetry, crash-diagnostics, security-engineering; 'data inventory, per-class retention, data-subject request flow'), the C-PRIVACY obligation already requires a deletion path, and it gates QA.CERT.privacy in milestones, so the proposal duplicates existing coverage.

findings.finding: Sweep: production pipeline (ship) and platform families. Physical-media SKUs (game card/cartridge, Blu-ray disc, gold master) appear nowhere. They impose engine-visible constraints: fixed ROM capacity tiers, read-only base content under a mandatory day-one patch (VFS precedence and patch-absent boot), a different seek/read profile for streaming budgets, disc install gating, and a lot-check/master submission artifact.
findings.evidence: Nintendo Switch game-card capacity tiers and update flow; PS5/Xbox disc install plus day-one patch practice; RES.PKG.ordering assumes access traces but names no physical target.
findings.proposed_change: Add BLD.REL.physical-media (packaging-release-patching; contributors package-formats-vfs, platform-console, certification-compliance): capacity budgeting, base+patch precedence tests including patch-absent boot, a media I/O profile in the hardware tiers, and the gold-master artifact. Mark it a variant of BLD.REL.store-variants.

verdict.reason: No physical-media/cartridge/disc/gold-master coverage exists, so the omission is real, but it is a niche SKU variant largely covered by confidential console packaging/patch stubs on BLD.REL.packaging; minor severity is right and it is marginal rather than material.

findings.target: UI.FW.architecture, legacy-patterns (polling UI binding), CORE.REFL.static-default, C-UI
findings.finding: UI.FW.architecture row text says UI view models are refreshed by per-frame property polling through string-keyed bindings. That is the banned legacy pattern. Skill purpose, C-UI and the catalogue stance say change-notified view models with load-time-resolved bindings. The generated docs propagate the wrong text.
findings.evidence: Unreal UMG property bindings poll per frame; MVVM toolkits use change notification. CORE.REFL.static-default forbids string lookup on runtime paths.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite the row: retained UI, reflected view models with change notification, bindings resolved at load/compile time to IDs/offsets, polling only as an explicit adapter for non-notifying sources.

verdict.reason: capabilities.json UI.FW.architecture literally says per-frame property polling through string-keyed bindings, contradicting the ui-architect purpose, C-UI, legacy L35 (which lists this very capability as the stance) and CORE.REFL.static-default; docs/01 propagates it and check.py's contradiction_terms scan doesn't catch it.

findings.finding: Nav yields intents and off-mesh special movement but nothing connects it to character movement. GAM.AI.links has no contributor and nav does not consume C-MOVE/C-CHARCTRL. No owner exists for nav-agent profiles matching the capsule and step/slope limits, nor for AI as a move-request source through the resimulatable move API. Mantle, climb and jump links have no executor.
findings.evidence: Unreal NavAgentProps synced with CharacterMovement and smart-link traversal via movement modes; Recast agent params must match the capsule or agents clip or stall.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.MOVE.ai-drive (character-movement; contributors navigation-pathfinding, ai-behavior-perception) and GAM.AI.agent-profiles (navigation-pathfinding; contributors character-movement, character-physics). Add character-movement as contributor of GAM.AI.links and GAM.AI.following. Document the intents-to-C-MOVE flow in C-MOVE.

verdict.reason: GAM.AI.links/following have no contributors, navigation-pathfinding consumes neither C-MOVE nor C-CHARCTRL, and no capability owns nav-agent profiles or AI as a move-request source; C-NAV says nav never moves bodies, so the executor gap is real and the contributor-based proposal avoids the upward-link rule.

findings.finding: Runtime player settings have a store and an editor-side schema editor but no owner for the settings screen model: schema-driven categories from C-CFG, apply/restart/dependency rules, timed display-mode revert, hardware-detected defaults, benchmark, reset, and platform-specific visibility.
findings.evidence: Unreal GameUserSettings and Lyra settings registry; Unity has none so each title rebuilds it; console cert rules on display-mode revert and safe defaults.
findings.proposed_change: Add UI.FW.settings-model (ui-architect; contributors persistence-save, runtime-scalability, accessibility, input-system, audio-architect) plus a preview tool. Require settings metadata (range, restart, dependency, platform visibility) on C-CFG entries.

verdict.reason: No settings-screen-model, display-mode revert or settings-metadata capability exists (GAM.SAVE.settings is a store, runtime-scalability owns only hardware auto-detect), but a settings menu is largely game-level UI content so major is inflated; minor/moderate.

findings.finding: No capability owns runtime active-locale management: OS locale detection, separate text/VO/subtitle language, fallback chains, live switch without restart re-resolving localized assets, fonts, VO packs and cached formatted text, and persistence of the choice.
findings.evidence: Store/cert expectation to honour system language; titles ship text in one language with VO in another; Unreal culture switching with localized asset re-resolution.
findings.proposed_change: Add UI.LOC.runtime-locale (localization-i18n; contributors persistence-save, audio-content-runtime, text-fonts, resource-streaming-architect, platform-architect) and define the locale-change event and reload obligations in C-LOC.

verdict.reason: C-LOC only mentions locale switching and PLAT.PAL.system-events only detects locale; no capability owns active-locale management, separate text/VO/subtitle language, re-resolution on live switch, or persistence of the choice.

findings.target: GAM.FW.local-players, INP.ACT.local-mp, UI.FW.focus, GAM.SAVE.settings, C-UI, C-CAMERA
findings.finding: Local multiplayer is promised by contracts (C-UI per-local-player roots and focus owners, C-CAMERA per-player rigs) but no capability implements it. GAM.FW.local-players lists only input-system. Per-viewport HUD/safe area, per-player subtitles, multi-focus navigation and per-local-player settings scope (accessibility, controls) are unowned; GAM.SAVE.settings scopes are only device/user/cloud.
findings.evidence: Couch co-op titles need per-player HUD, rebinding, assists and controller-to-user pairing.
findings.proposed_change: Add UI.FW.local-player-ui (ui-architect; contributors gameplay-architect, gameplay-camera, render-architect, accessibility). Add contributors ui-architect, gameplay-camera, persistence-save, accessibility to GAM.FW.local-players. Add a per-local-player scope to GAM.SAVE.settings and C-A11YRT settings.

verdict.reason: GAM.FW.local-players has only input-system as contributor, UI.FW.focus likewise, and C-UI/C-CAMERA promise per-local-player roots and rigs that the milestone exit (2-player split-screen with independent UI focus) requires but no capability implements.

findings.target: tool_consumes of text-fonts, facial-animation, cinematics-sequencer, ik-procedural-animation, animation-runtime, gameplay-data, ui-architect, crowd-simulation
findings.finding: Skills that own cook-time builders, importers or viewport tools declare no matching contract, and check.py only requires any tool contract. text-fonts (font subsetting) has empty tool_consumes; facial-animation (capture import, per-locale lip-sync bake) lacks C-IMPORT/C-COOK; cinematics-sequencer (take recorder, movie render, preload) lacks C-COOK/C-IMPORT/C-EDVIEW; gameplay-data (spreadsheet round-trip, table cook) lacks C-IMPORT/C-COOK; rigging, 2D rigging, sequencer and facial tools lack C-EDVIEW; UI.TOOL.preview lacks C-EDPREVIEW.
findings.evidence: The framework's own rule that the format owner owns the builder and the pipeline hosts it through C-COOK; without the edge the tools configuration proof cannot show the builder reaches the host.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-COOK to text-fonts, facial-animation, cinematics-sequencer, gameplay-data, crowd-simulation; C-IMPORT to facial-animation, cinematics-sequencer, gameplay-data; C-EDVIEW to ik-procedural-animation, animation-runtime, facial-animation, cinematics-sequencer; C-EDPREVIEW to ik-procedural-animation, facial-animation, ui-architect. Extend check.py to derive required tool contracts from tool-capability contributors.

verdict.reason: text-fonts has empty tool_consumes while owning font-subsetting, and facial-animation, cinematics-sequencer and gameplay-data lack the cook/import edges the finding lists, while check.py only demands any tool contract; some proposed edges (e.g. crowd-simulation C-COOK) are speculative but the core wiring gap is real.

findings.finding: Only generated dialogue scenes get per-locale retiming. Hand-authored cutscenes with VO have no capability for locale variant audio/subtitle/viseme tracks, duration reconciliation when localized VO is longer, or per-locale validation. C-SEQ consumes C-LOC only optionally.
findings.evidence: German/Russian VO routinely exceeds English timing; Unreal Sequencer localized audio and subtitle tracks; per-language lip-sync in large narrative titles.
findings.proposed_change: Add ANM.CINE.localized-tracks (cinematics-sequencer; contributors localization-i18n, audio-content-runtime, facial-animation, narrative-dialogue) with duration policy and per-locale validation; make locale variant handling part of C-SEQ.

verdict.reason: Only GAM.NARR.scenes carries per-locale retiming; no ANM.CINE capability or validation covers locale variant audio/subtitle/viseme tracks or duration reconciliation for hand-authored cutscenes, and C-SEQ consumes C-LOC only optionally.

findings.finding: Navigation data as a streamed, world-partitioned layer is unowned: per-cell navmesh cook and streaming, cross-cell stitching and hierarchical graphs, server residency without rendering, invoker-style regional generation, and dynamic invalidation from destruction/building/voxel edits. GAM.AI.navmesh has no contributors, C-NAV consumes C-WORLD optionally, and PHY.DEST.propagation's update to navigation has no receiving capability.
findings.evidence: Unreal World Partition navmesh streaming and nav invokers; large open-world titles stream nav tiles with world cells.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.AI.nav-streaming (navigation-pathfinding; contributors world-architect, world-data-model, destruction-fracture, voxel-worlds, resource-streaming-architect), tagged openworld and sandbox; add a dynamic-invalidation input to C-NAV.

verdict.reason: GAM.AI.navmesh has no contributors and there is no capability for per-cell nav streaming/stitching or a receiver for PHY.DEST.propagation's nav update; WLD.PART.activation lists navigation as contributor only for bulk registration, so the gap is largely but not wholly open.

findings.finding: Localized strings embedding an input action must resolve at runtime to a per-device glyph or per-locale key name and re-resolve on device change. INP.ACT.glyphs has no contributors and neither rich text nor message formatting names an action-glyph argument.
findings.evidence: Standard practice: Unreal Common UI input-action rich text, Steam Input glyph APIs.
findings.proposed_change: Add ui-architect, text-fonts, localization-i18n as contributors of INP.ACT.glyphs and a typed input-action argument in UI.LOC.messageformat and UI.TXT.rich, visible to gather and validation.

verdict.reason: INP.ACT.glyphs has no contributors and neither UI.TXT.rich nor UI.LOC.messageformat names an input-action argument; a valid minor cross-owner interface omission with a sound proposal.

findings.finding: No capability covers player-facing audio mix options: category volume presets, mono downmix, dialogue/speech boost, per-output dynamic-range profiles (TV, headphones, handheld) and speaker-layout selection.
findings.evidence: Xbox Accessibility Guidelines audio guidance; console loudness targets; EBU R128 device profiles.
findings.proposed_change: Add AUD.DSP.user-mix (audio-dsp-mixing; contributors accessibility, persistence-save, platform-architect) exposed as C-CFG settings with an accessibility validation case.

verdict.reason: No capability covers player-facing mix options (mono downmix, dialogue boost, per-output dynamic-range profiles); AUD.DSP.dynamics and AUD.ARCH.routing address loudness and endpoints only, so a minor omission with a sound C-CFG-based proposal.

findings.finding: The minimal profile is defined as narrative-centric, yet facial-animation is lite3d/std3d only. Dialogue-driven 2D portrait or sprite mouth animation per locale has no owner.
findings.evidence: Visual-novel and 2D dialogue games use viseme-driven sprite/Spine attachment swaps.
findings.proposed_change: Add ANM.RT.2d-speech (animation-runtime; contributors facial-animation, narrative-dialogue, audio-content-runtime) tagged minimal and min2d, driven by C-DIALOGUE timing.

verdict.reason: minimal is defined as narrative-centric, facial-animation is lite3d/std3d only, and ANM.RT.2d has no speech-driven sprite/viseme capability, so 2D dialogue mouth animation is unowned; niche but a real scale-down hole.

findings.finding: Motion reduction/photosensitivity (accessibility) and camera comfort motion options (gameplay-camera) overlap; UI.A11Y.motion has no contributors though camera shake, UI transitions, post effects, VFX and cue flash/hit-stop all consume it. No canonical reduced-motion and flash-limit setting contract or runtime flash limiter is stated.
findings.evidence: Game Accessibility Guidelines; WCAG 2.3 flash thresholds; C-VIEW already assigns shake scaling to C-CAMERA, so the split is partial.
findings.proposed_change: Make UI.A11Y.motion sole setting owner with contributors gameplay-camera, ui-architect, post-color-hdr, vfx-particles, gameplay-systems-toolkit; reword GAM.CAM.comfort as consumption; add a runtime flash-limiter hook tested by QA.CERT.photosensitivity.

verdict.reason: UI.A11Y.motion has no contributors, GAM.CAM.comfort duplicates part of it, and no runtime flash limiter exists beyond QA.CERT.photosensitivity testing; note vfx-particles consumes only C-A11Y so adding it as a UI.A11Y contributor would trip check.py's C-A11YRT rule and needs a consume edge, but the proposal is fixable.

findings.target: XC.DET.conformance, C-DET, determinism-replay, simulation-validation, M0 gate
findings.finding: Determinism conformance matrix (toolchain x ISA x platform x cores x schedule) is owned by determinism-replay, the implementer of C-DET; simulation-validation disclaims matrix definition. The oracle for the most critical property is defined by the implementer, contradicting L56 and QA.AGENT.oracle-independence. M0 gate validator is QA.ROBUST.concurrency, which does not exercise cross-ISA/compiler equality.
findings.evidence: Lockstep/rollback engines rely on an independent state-hash oracle across toolchains; the framework's own rule forbids implementers controlling their oracles.
findings.proposed_change: Move matrix definition and golden hash corpus to simulation-validation (QA.SIM.determinism-matrix); determinism-replay keeps policy and hooks. Re-point M0 gate validator to QA.SIM.golden-traces plus cross-ISA differential lane with a known-red canary (FMA/reduction-order change).

verdict.reason: XC.DET.conformance is owned by determinism-replay, simulation-validation lists 'Determinism matrix definition' as a non-responsibility, and the M0 validator QA.ROBUST.concurrency is schedule stress, not cross-ISA/compiler equality; C-DET's suite already has an independent oracle_author, so the real defect is matrix ownership plus the mis-pointed gate.

findings.target: milestones.json gates (M0 mutation-gate, XC.DET.conformance, key-custody; M1 QA.RENDER.golden, QA.SIM.stability-suite, QA.SIM.netsim, XC.SEC.threats; M2 soak, pacing-latency; M3 reference-validation; M4 NET.SRV.transactions, XC.SEC.incident; M5 RES.MGMT.validation; M6 cross-server, XC.SEC.sandbox; M7 compat-corpus, release-criteria)
findings.finding: Many gate validators do not exercise the gated property: mutation gate validated by fuzzing; golden images by HW compat matrix; physics stability by soak; netsim and reference path tracer by paperwork oracle-change-control; idempotent transactions and hand-off by load tests; streaming oracle by load-time analysis instead of QA.SIM.streaming; key custody/incident/hardening by cert pre-checks; sandbox and vuln-response by fuzzing; M7 chain circular (compat-corpus validated by a migration process; release-criteria validated only at M7 yet used as validator from M1).
findings.evidence: A validator must be able to fail when the property breaks (mutation/canary principle in QA.AGENT.gate-canaries); check.py only proves the validator exists.
findings.proposed_change: Add per-gate fields exercised_by and known_red; check.py rule that the validator lane relates to the gated capability's family/contract. Re-point: golden/stability to gate-canaries seeded defects, transactions/cross-server to QA.ROBUST.distributed-faults/QA.SIM.server-dst, streaming to QA.SIM.streaming, M7 release-criteria to an independent rehearsal.

verdict.reason: Every listed gate/validator pair exists as stated (mutation-gate by fuzzing, golden by compat, stability by soak, transactions/cross-server by load, RES.MGMT.validation by load-time despite QA.SIM.streaming existing, M7 compat-corpus/release-criteria circular-ish), and check.py only proves validator existence, non-ownership and gate cycles, not relevance to the gated property.

findings.target: milestones M1, M3, M5, M6, M7 exits vs gates
findings.finding: Exit criteria promise outcomes with no gate: M1 save/localization/accessibility/hot reload; M3 both GPU-driven and CPU-submission paths; M5 XR on PC/standalone/console and massim desync; M6 persistence crash-consistency with 1k bots, distributed cook, AAA slice; M7 console certification pass. M5 has 3 gates, M6 has 4.
findings.evidence: Ungated exit clauses are decided by the orchestrator's judgment, defeating independent validation.
findings.proposed_change: Add gate rows per exit clause with independent validators (UI.A11Y.validation, RND.GEO.cpu-submission via QA.RENDER.matrix on lite tier, XR motion-to-photon hardware capture + OpenXR CTS, QA.ROBUST.distributed-faults for persistence, QA.CERT.platform dry-run submission); add a check that named capabilities in exit sentences are gated.

verdict.reason: M3 CPU/GPU-driven paths, M5 XR and massim desync, M6 persistence crash-consistency/distributed cook, and M7 console certification have no gate rows (M5 has 3, M6 has 4); only the M1 items are partially covered by the QA.REF.ladder gate.

findings.target: oracle_reference of 55 contracts (C-WORLD, C-MATIF, C-TEMPORAL, C-SVC, C-SCRIPT, C-COOK, C-BUILD, C-PKG, C-GI, C-LIGHT, C-XRVIEW, C-SHARD, C-SRVDATA, C-VCS, C-VEHICLE, C-AI, C-CHARCTRL, and 38 more)
findings.finding: 55 of ~125 code contracts carry the identical placeholder oracle_reference 'reference scenes or analytic cases declared in the conformance suite; derived goldens are regression-only', naming no oracle. It is circular (oracle author declares its own references) and gives an autonomous oracle author nothing to anchor to, although external references exist.
findings.evidence: OpenXR CTS (C-XRVIEW); furnace/analytic radiance and external renderers Mitsuba/pbrt (C-GI, C-LIGHT, C-PTREF); Jepsen/TLA+ and idempotency oracles (C-SHARD, C-SRVDATA); provider sandbox traces (C-SVC, C-LIVE, C-VCS); reproducible-build comparison (C-BUILD, C-COOK); test262-class script conformance (C-SCRIPT); supersampled ground truth sequences (C-TEMPORAL); ISO 3888 manoeuvres (C-VEHICLE).
findings.proposed_change: Ban the placeholder in check.py; require each oracle_reference to name a non-derived source class (analytic, external implementation, standard suite, simplified model) with reference_status available/to-build; to-build items get a capability owner.

verdict.reason: Exactly 55 contracts carry the identical placeholder oracle_reference and check.py only requires the list be non-empty, so an oracle author gets no external anchor for contracts like C-XRVIEW, C-GI, C-SCRIPT, C-BUILD.

findings.target: functional-automation-soak, robustness-fuzzing, oracle_author assignments; C-IO, C-COOK, C-BUILD, C-PKG, C-EDCMD, C-VCS, C-SCRIPT, C-SAVE, C-SRVDATA, C-ML, C-MLGPU, C-PRESENT, C-FRAME
findings.finding: functional-automation-soak (bots/soak expertise) is oracle author for 34 contracts across IO, VFS, cook, build, packaging, editor, VCS, script VM, save, server persistence, service emulators and never consumes 31 of them; ~100 of ~130 contracts have oracle authors that neither consume nor implement them (unchecked). robustness-fuzzing authors 19 contracts including semantic ones (C-ML, C-MLGPU, C-PRESENT, C-FLOW, C-FRAME, C-RELOAD, C-REFL) where a fuzz corpus finds crashes, not semantic violations.
findings.evidence: One SKILL.md agent cannot hold 34 unrelated suites or the build-system/distributed-persistence/editor literatures; the framework's own split rule is different literatures.
findings.proposed_change: Split into a tool/pipeline conformance skill (C-ASSET, C-COOK, C-BUILD, C-PKG, C-VFS, C-EDCMD, C-EDHOST, C-GRAPH, C-EDVIEW, C-VCS, C-CMD, C-IMPORT, C-EDIT) and a server/persistence/service conformance skill (C-SERVER, C-SRVDATA, C-SVC, C-LIVE, C-SAVE); move C-ML/C-MLGPU to foundation-conformance or render-validation and C-PRESENT/C-FLOW/C-FRAME to perf-benchmarking or simulation-validation; add a validates/consume edge and a check.py rule.

verdict.reason: functional-automation-soak is oracle author for 34 contracts and consumes only C-GAME?/C-INPUT?/C-NET?/C-AUTOMATION (31 unconsumed), its purpose text does not mention IO/cook/build/VCS/persistence, and robustness-fuzzing authors semantic contracts such as C-ML, C-MLGPU, C-PRESENT; the split rule in docs/00 supports the proposal.

findings.finding: L69 (retry until green; quarantines hiding nondeterminism) names QA.STRAT.flaky as its stance, but QA.STRAT.flaky defines automatic quarantine after repeated failures and rerun-based clearing with quarantined tests excluded from gates, which is the legacy pattern. selection-policy says determinism/conformance/holdout lanes are never skipped, not never quarantined; test-integrity omits quarantine. Quarantining is the cheapest way for an autonomous agent to green a gate, and for races/desyncs intermittency is the signal.
findings.evidence: Google/Microsoft flaky-test studies: many flakes are real races; L69's own default stance is root-cause policy.
findings.proposed_change: Reword QA.STRAT.flaky: reruns never clear failures in determinism, concurrency, conformance, holdout, fuzz-regression, netsim lanes; quarantine requires owner, expiry, global budget counted by test-integrity, recorded seed, and blocks release-criteria.

verdict.reason: QA.STRAT.flaky literally defines automatic quarantine and rerun-based clearing with quarantined tests excluded from gates while L69 names it as the stance against 'retries or quarantines that hide nondeterminism', a direct self-contradiction that lets agents green gates cheaply.

findings.target: QA.STRAT.contract-fakes; test_double contracts (C-SVC, C-LIVE, C-VCS, C-INTEGRITY, C-SIGN, C-XRVIEW, C-VIDEO, C-DEVICE, C-SHARD, C-SRVDATA)
findings.finding: Test doubles are verified only against the contract's conformance suite, which for C-SVC, C-LIVE, C-VCS, C-INTEGRITY, C-XRVIEW has no real-provider reference, so the double is checked against the text it was built from. No drift lane runs the suite against the real provider (platform sandbox, Perforce, OpenXR runtimes, real KMS).
findings.evidence: Consumer-driven contract testing (Pact provider verification) and Google's verified-fakes practice exist because fakes drift; Steam/PSN/EOS/OpenXR/Perforce change independently.
findings.proposed_change: Add real_backend_lane (sandbox, cadence, drift ticket) to boundary contracts and a periodic real-vs-double differential to QA.STRAT.contract-fakes; extend check.py.

verdict.reason: QA.STRAT.contract-fakes only requires doubles to pass the contract's own conformance suite, and C-SVC, C-LIVE, C-VCS, C-INTEGRITY, C-XRVIEW all carry the placeholder oracle_reference, so no real-provider drift lane exists anywhere in the data.

findings.finding: Image validation is single-frame (FLIP-class golden, present capture). No sequence-based validation of TAA, upscalers, denoisers, frame generation, motion vectors and disocclusion (ghosting, flicker, shimmer); C-TEMPORAL has the placeholder oracle_reference.
findings.evidence: Temporal artifacts are the main failure mode of DLSS/FSR/XeSS and RT denoisers, assessed with video metrics (FovVideoVDP, temporal FLIP) against supersampled ground-truth sequences and reprojection-error tests.
findings.proposed_change: Add QA.RENDER.temporal (render-validation): scripted camera paths, supersampled reference sequences, temporal metrics, motion-vector reprojection error; make it C-TEMPORAL's oracle_reference and gate at M3.

verdict.reason: QA.RENDER.golden and final-frame are single-frame FLIP/present capture, nothing in the data mentions sequence, ghosting, flicker or temporal metrics, and C-TEMPORAL has the placeholder oracle_reference, while temporal artifacts are the main upscaler/denoiser failure mode.

findings.target: NET.ARCH.validation, UI.A11Y.validation, RND.PT.reference, CNT.COOK.determinism-check, RND.SHADER.precision, RND.RHI.*-validation
findings.finding: Unlike other validation capabilities marked 'hooks only', these are owned by the implementing skill and define scenarios and thresholds (network-architect owns acceptance thresholds with co-sign only; accessibility validates its own features; path-tracing owns the ground-truth oracle; cook determinism and shader precision self-verified; RHI backends own conformance runs). This is L56 implementer-owned validation.
findings.evidence: Framework rule: implementers must not control the oracles that judge them; thresholds set by the judged party drift loose.
findings.proposed_change: Apply the hooks-only wording; move thresholds/suites to simulation-validation, ui-text-conformance, render-validation or the new tool-conformance skill; backend skills only run suites and own hooks.

verdict.reason: The contracts these capabilities sit under already have independent oracle authors (C-NET/C-REP sim-validation, C-A11YRT ui-text-conformance, C-PTREF/C-RHI/C-SHADER render-validation, C-COOK functional-automation-soak), QA.RENDER.reference-validation and QA.RENDER.shader-conformance independently validate the path tracer and shader precision, NET.ARCH.validation is co-signed, and domain owners defining scenarios is a recorded design choice backed by QA.AGENT.oracle-change-control.

findings.target: milestones contracts_frozen, C-TEST, crosscutting independence matrix
findings.finding: Nothing requires the conformance suite, sealed holdout and known-red canary to exist before a contract freezes (check.py proves only freeze order). The independence matrix pairs test-architect with owning-skill, but test-architect is the oracle author of no contract; the real oracle-author pairs and the gate-validator vs gated-owner pair are absent.
findings.evidence: L56 requires tests before features; the workstream separation currently holds only by assignment accident.
findings.proposed_change: Add freeze_requires (suite v1, holdout sealed, canary red, reference implementation passes) to freezes and check.py; generate matrix pairs from contracts.json oracle_author and add the gate-validator pair.

verdict.reason: check.py proves only freeze ordering plus oracle-author-built-before-freeze, no data requires suite/holdout/canary before freeze, and test-architect is oracle author of no contract so the independence pair 'test-architect vs owning-skill' is stale (though per-contract independence is in fact machine-checked, making it a minor gap).

findings.finding: Labelled E while parents QA.AGENT.holdout, oracle-independence and mutation-gate are M; anti-probing protocol for LLM implementers has no established production practice.
findings.evidence: Holdout hygiene against agent overfitting is novel (benchmark-contamination literature); no shipped engine runs it.
findings.proposed_change: Relabel M and add a radar entry with fallback (human-audited holdouts).

verdict.reason: QA.AGENT.holdout-hygiene is E while holdout, oracle-independence and mutation-gate are M and the radar entry for agent test-side validation omits it; an anti-probing protocol for LLM implementers has no production precedent, so relabel to M with radar coverage is sound.

findings.finding: Learned-component validation covers runtime numeric parity only; no owner for model quality/behavior regression (neural animation, learned denoisers, LLM barks, physics surrogates): held-out eval sets, statistical thresholds, drift.
findings.evidence: Behavior regresses with identical numerics after quantization or retraining; these features are M/X on the radar.
findings.proposed_change: Add QA.SIM.learned-eval (simulation-validation, M) with per-feature eval sets and statistical thresholds, gating any M/X ML feature entering a shipping profile.

verdict.reason: ML.RT.validation already names 'backend & quantization conformance with tolerance tables; model-version regression', so the claim that only runtime numeric parity is covered is not fully accurate, and the remaining gap (per-feature quality eval sets) is a speculative minor addition on M/X features with radar fallbacks.

findings.finding: Three owners run hardware matrices with no rule for device-set selection; nothing derives the matrix from PLAT.PAL.device-db tiers and PRF.METH.field telemetry (share, driver deny-list).
findings.evidence: Real GPU/driver matrices are chosen by share and defect history or they grow unbounded or miss failing devices.
findings.proposed_change: Single matrix definition generated from the device DB by tier and share; render, functional and perf lanes consume it.

verdict.reason: QA.FUNC.compat, QA.RENDER.matrix and BLD.CI.device-lanes each run device matrices, ARCH.REQ.platform-matrix covers only OS x ISA x API, and nothing derives device sets from PLAT.PAL.device-db tiers or PRF.METH.field share/deny-list data; minor operational gap correctly rated.

findings.target: user-images, replicated-state, client-rpcs, replays, cloud-saves, RND.TEX.runtime-decode, texture-streaming-vt, ui-architect
findings.finding: user-images is validated by ui-architect but the decoder (RND.TEX.runtime-decode) is owned by texture-streaming-vt, which has no untrusted_inputs and is not a parser_owner. Image limits cannot be enforced by a UI framework skill. replicated-state, client-rpcs, replays and cloud-saves are deserialized via serialization-schema but list no parser owner, unlike packets and saves.
findings.evidence: libwebp CVE-2023-4863 and stb/libpng-class decoder bugs were reached via player-supplied images; the parser owner must carry the harness. Verified: texture-streaming-vt untrusted_inputs is empty.
findings.proposed_change: Set user-images validating_owner to texture-streaming-vt (ui-architect as consumer/parser_owner) and add it to that skill's untrusted_inputs. Add serialization-schema as parser_owner of replicated-state, client-rpcs, replays and cloud-saves.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: user-images is validated by ui-architect with empty parser_owners, RND.TEX.runtime-decode is owned by texture-streaming-vt whose untrusted_inputs is empty, and replicated-state, client-rpcs, replays and cloud-saves all have empty parser_owners; the fix is sound and check.py's registration rule would enforce it.

findings.finding: cloud-saves is labeled semi-trusted-signed, which is wrong if the signer is client-held or client-derivable, since the local user can re-sign edited saves. GAM.SAVE.integrity never states key location or that signed saves cannot be authority for online economy or ranked state.
findings.evidence: Client-side save HMAC keys are routinely extracted; Diablo III and Destiny moved progression server-side for this reason.
findings.proposed_change: Label cloud-saves hostile-local unless signed by a server-held key under XC.SEC.key-custody. Add to GAM.SAVE.integrity: client-signed saves are tamper-evident only, and online-relevant fields are server-authoritative via NET.SRV.persistence. Add anti-cheat-integrity as contributor.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: cloud-saves is semi-trusted-signed, GAM.SAVE.integrity is just 'Save signing & tamper policy' with security-engineering only, and XC.SEC.key-custody says only 'no agent-held keys', so client-held signer and non-authority of signed saves are unstated; labeling and server-authority obligations are sound.

findings.finding: GPU-side memory safety is missing: RND.SHADER.untrusted covers only GPU-DoS limits. Nothing covers zero-initialization of fresh and aliased VRAM, robust (bounds-checked) buffer/image access for untrusted shaders, or device-lost/TDR recovery after a UGC-triggered hang.
findings.evidence: WebGPU mandates zero-init and robust access; LeftoverLocals (2023) leaked GPU local memory across processes; Vulkan robustBufferAccess2; render-graph aliasing reuses memory without clears.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.MEM.zero-init-robust-access (owner gpu-memory-resources; contributors shader-system, render-graph-scheduling, security-engineering). Extend ugc-graphs limits with device-lost recovery and robust access; add a UGC-hang device-lost scenario to the M6 sandbox gate.

verdict.reason: Zero-init and robust access have no capability and RND.SHADER.untrusted is only GPU-DoS limits, though device-lost recovery is partly covered by RND.RHI.crash so that sub-claim is overstated; the core omission is real and material for UGC shaders.

findings.finding: The cloud render host has a video/input back-channel and multi-tenant GPU packing, but remote input, session-control messages and tenant identity are not registered inputs (no validating owner, limits or fuzz target). Tenant isolation appears only as a side-channel row in XC.SEC.hardening.
findings.evidence: Cloud-gaming hosts (GeForce NOW, Xbox Cloud Gaming) treat remote input and session control as pre-auth network input with per-session isolation.
findings.proposed_change: Add registry input remote-play-input (hostile-remote, validating owner platform-architect, parser_owners input-system and network-transport, limits rate/schema/session-token). Add per-session process/GPU-context isolation as an explicit XC.SEC.hardening obligation of the capability.

verdict.reason: No remote-play-input registry entry exists and tenant isolation is only a side-channel row in XC.SEC.hardening, but the capability is maturity M, opt-in with a revisit trigger and third-party-stream fallback, so major is inflated and minor fits.

findings.finding: BLD.SYS.third-party is a single line. Dependency admission by autonomous agents is unspecified: no internal mirror/allow-list, hash-pinned lockfile, human gate for new dependencies or maintainer changes, or upstream-diff review on update. Agents that hallucinate package names create a squatting path.
findings.evidence: Package-name hallucination ('slopsquatting', 2025), xz-utils backdoor (2024), dependency confusion (Birsan 2021).
findings.proposed_change: Extend BLD.SYS.third-party with an admission policy: mirror-only egress, hash-pinned lockfile, new-dependency and maintainer-change human gate registered in ARCH.ORG.human-gates, vendored-diff review. Contributors ci-cd-automation and program-orchestration.

verdict.reason: BLD.SYS.third-party is one line and no admission policy, human gate for new dependencies or slopsquatting control exists (existing XC.SEC.supply-chain, BLD.SYS.provenance and third-party-source 'pinned/verified' cover SBOM/provenance only), so agent-driven dependency admission is a real gap.

findings.finding: No capability governs security-relevant gameplay randomness. CORE.MATH.random is deterministic counter-based. Nothing requires server-authoritative loot, shuffle, matchmaking or gacha outcomes to use an unpredictable CSPRNG, forbids replicating seeds before use, or makes odds auditable.
findings.evidence: Seed-recovery attacks on Mersenne-Twister-class generators in online games; PLAT.COMM.disclosure odds obligations are unenforceable without an audit record.
findings.proposed_change: Add XC.SEC.gameplay-rng (owner anti-cheat-integrity; contributors security-runtime, math-simd-numerics, server-scaleout-persistence, determinism-replay): economy/ranking outcomes use server CSPRNG with an audit record; deterministic streams only where C-DET requires and seeds not disclosed early.

verdict.reason: No capability requires unpredictable server RNG or audit for economy outcomes (CORE.MATH.random is deterministic, CORE.TYPES.crypto only wraps CSPRNG), but loot/gacha design is largely game code per docs/06 C.2, so an engine-level obligation is real but minor rather than major.

findings.finding: Player-controlled identity strings (display names, clan tags, lobby/world names, UGC titles) are not a registered input; chat-text limits are length/rate only. No mandate for NFC normalization, stripping bidi override and zero-width controls, confusable checks, or context-specific escaping in UI, logs and filenames.
findings.evidence: Trojan Source (CVE-2021-42574) bidi spoofing; homoglyph impersonation; name-based injection in game lobbies.
findings.proposed_change: Add input player-profile-strings (hostile-remote, validating owner online-services-liveops, parser_owners text-fonts and ui-architect, limits length, normalization, control-character allow-list, output-context escaping).

verdict.reason: Confirmed: no player-profile-strings input exists, chat-text and server-list-entries limits are length/rate only and nothing mandates normalization or bidi/confusable handling; a minor, in-mandate addition with a sound proposal.

findings.finding: Server-side player data at rest is unowned: no encryption at rest, backup and point-in-time-restore retention, or erasure propagation through backups and analytics stores. ED.COLLAB.backup covers only dev infrastructure while support-tools restoration presumes backups exist.
findings.evidence: GDPR Art. 17 erasure and Art. 32 security of processing apply to backups.
findings.proposed_change: Add NET.SRV.backup-retention (owner server-scaleout-persistence; contributors privacy-data-protection, security-engineering, online-services-liveops) covering KMS-backed encryption and deletion-through-backup semantics, referenced from XC.SEC.data-rights.

verdict.reason: Backup/KMS/retention of server-side data is backend service operation, which docs/06 C.3 declares out of engine scope (engine owns only the integration boundary), and XC.SEC.data-rights already carries retention and data-subject request flow, so this contradicts a recorded scope decision without new evidence.

findings.finding: Server-side crash ingestion, minidump processing and symbolication parse hostile-remote input while holding symbols, builds and credentials, but no capability requires sandboxed, least-privilege workers separate from the symbol store; registry limits are size/rate only.
findings.evidence: Minidump-stackwalk and Breakpad processor parser CVEs; Crashpad server ingestion is conventionally sandboxed.
findings.proposed_change: Add to OBS.CRASH.pipeline an obligation that processors run as sandboxed, ephemeral, least-privilege workers; add crash-diagnostics and observability-telemetry as parser_owners and extend limits to 'size/rate; sandboxed processing'.

verdict.reason: Server-side ingestion workers are backend infrastructure per docs/06 C.3, and the proposal is unsound because crash-diagnostics already validates crash-uploads and observability-telemetry validates telemetry-batches, so naming them as parser_owners is redundant/incoherent.
